F301.role: Gastroenterology referral vetting nurse: a specialist nurse in a hospital outpatient department who vets each incoming GP referral and decides its pathway, format and priority.
F301.setting: A district general hospital gastroenterology outpatient service receives electronic referrals from primary care. Each referral arrives as a structured record built from the referrer's form, the extracted patient summary, attached investigation results and the hospital's own contact history. The vetting nurse reviews one referral at a time against local protocols. These include a suspected-cancer fast-track (for example iron deficiency anaemia at age 60 or over, faecal immunochemical test of 10 or above, or progressive dysphagia). Before booking, the nurse decides whether the referral is complete and consistent, how urgent the need is, and which first-contact format fits.

fast_track_met.instructions: Referral meets the clinic's suspected-cancer fast-track criteria as documented.

vetting_outcome.instructions: What should the vetting nurse do with this referral now?

criteria.return_to_referrer: Decline with advice; problem outside remit or already managed elsewhere.
criteria.hold_for_info: Pause vetting; one required result or clarification still outstanding.
criteria.accept_routine: Book standard slot; information sufficient and no urgent features confirmed.
criteria.accept_expedited: Book earliest or fast-track slot; urgent features confirmed by record.

first_contact.instructions: Which first-contact format best suits this referral?

criteria.advice_letter: Written guidance to referrer; question answerable without seeing patient.
criteria.telephone_review: Remote consultant call; history needed but no examination required.
criteria.nurse_clinic: Nurse-led protocol appointment for straightforward, low-comorbidity presentations.
criteria.consultant_clinic: Face-to-face consultant visit; examination or multiple comorbidities need assessment.
criteria.straight_to_test: Book endoscopy directly; criteria met and patient fit for procedure.

clinical_urgency.instructions: How urgent is the clinical need for specialist review?
criteria: Routine: stable symptoms, no red-flag features recorded
Soon: deterioration documented within eight weeks, no red flags
Urgent: one red-flag feature not explained by results
Very urgent: unexplained red flag plus abnormal bloods or rapid decline

record_agreement.instructions: How closely do details agree across the referral's sections?
criteria: Two or more material mismatches between sections
Exactly one material mismatch between sections
Only trivial mismatches such as spelling or rounding
All corresponding values agree across every section

factors.name: presenting_problem
factors.description: Main complaint driving the referral; sets which protocol thresholds and red flags apply.

factors.name: red_flag_count
factors.description: Number of genuine red-flag features (weight loss, anaemia, progressive dysphagia, palpable mass, FIT at or above 10) supported by the record.

factors.name: benign_explanation
factors.description: Whether the record holds a credible benign explanation for the alarming signal, such as normal colonoscopy within two years, confirmed haemorrhoids, or anaemia explained by menorrhagia under gynaecology.

factors.name: results_status
factors.description: State of the investigations the protocol requires: all recent, some pending, older than three months, or none attached.

factors.name: mismatch_severity
factors.description: Size of disagreement between corresponding values in different sections, from none through trivial (spelling, rounding) to material (value changes protocol eligibility).

factors.name: mismatch_site
factors.description: Where the main mismatch sits: age in demographics vs note, a value quoted in note vs lab result, red-flag checklist vs note, medication list vs note, or dates vs contact history.

factors.name: sequence_anomaly
factors.description: A date shows events out of order, such as a referral sent before the result it quotes was collected, or symptom onset recorded after the referral date.

factors.name: symptom_trajectory
factors.description: Course of symptoms over recent weeks as recorded in the clinical section: stable, slowly worsening, or rapid decline.

factors.name: prior_contact
factors.description: Relevant hospital history: none, recent normal investigation, discharged from this clinic within 12 months, or an open episode with another service.

factors.name: comorbidity_burden
factors.description: Count of significant comorbidities (anticoagulation, heart failure, frailty, renal impairment) affecting fitness for direct endoscopy and choice of format.

factors.name: threshold_boundary
factors.description: A key value sits exactly on or within rounding of a protocol cut-off (age 60, FIT 10, ferritin limit), leaving eligibility arguable.

factors.name: referrer_urgency_label
factors.description: Referrer ticked urgent on the form, independent of clinical content; a decoy that may or may not be supported.

factors.name: advice_only_request
factors.description: Referrer's actual question could be answered in writing (for example a medication query) without an appointment.

sections.name: referral
sections.description: Identifiers, sent date, referrer details, requested priority, and short free-text reason for referral.

sections.name: patient
sections.description: Date of birth, stated age, sex, comorbidities list, current medications.

sections.name: clinical
sections.description: Symptom list with onset dates, trajectory, referrer-ticked red-flag checklist, weight change, short examination note.

sections.name: investigations
sections.description: List of results with test, value, unit, reference range, collected date and status; may be null.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Prior hospital contacts, procedures, discharges and open episodes, with dates and one-line outcome summaries.

F301.rendering_notes: Free text: referral.reason_text (two or three sentences from the referrer), clinical.exam_note (one sentence), and history[].outcome_summary (one line per contact). presenting_problem appears in referral.reason_text and clinical.symptoms; it is never a labelled category field. red_flag_count is shown indirectly through symptom entries, weight change in kg over months, investigation values against reference ranges, and phrases in reason_text. The clinical.red_flags_ticked checklist is filled by the referrer and may overstate or understate. benign_explanation appears as a history entry (normal colonoscopy with date), an investigations entry, or a line in reason_text such as 'known haemorrhoids, under gynae for heavy periods'; it is never labelled as mitigation. results_status: complete_recent gives dated results within 90 days of referral.sent_date; partial_pending includes entries with status 'pending' and value null; stale gives collected dates older than 90 days; absent sets investigations to null or an empty list. mismatch_severity and mismatch_site place disagreements unannounced, for example: patient.age 59 vs date of birth giving 60; Hb quoted as 98 in reason_text vs 108 g/L in results; checklist ticks weight loss while clinical.weight_change_kg is 0; medication list omits an anticoagulant mentioned in exam_note; reason_text says 'never scoped' while history lists a colonoscopy. Trivial mismatches are name spelling, unit rounding (11.9 vs 12) or reordered initials. sequence_anomaly shows as referral.sent_date earlier than a quoted result's collected_date, or symptom onset after sent_date. symptom_trajectory appears via dated symptom entries and reason_text wording. prior_contact appears only in the history list. comorbidity_burden appears in patient.comorbidities and medications. threshold_boundary sets a value exactly at a cut-off. referrer_urgency_label sets referral.priority_requested to 'urgent'; this is a decoy and must not decide answers alone. advice_only_request shows as a question in reason_text such as 'please advise on stopping PPI'. Decoy fields: priority_requested, red_flags_ticked, and alarming words in reason_text. No record ever contains a triage outcome, urgency rating, format choice, eligibility flag or agreement score.

F302.role: Site eligibility reviewer at a multi-site clinical trial unit, checking each completed screening visit record before a subject may be randomised
F302.setting: After a screening visit, the site enters consent, demographics, visit timing, laboratory results, eligibility criterion checks and concomitant medications into the trial's electronic data capture system. The reviewer opens one subject's screening record at a time. They reconcile the sections against each other and against protocol thresholds and windows. They then decide whether eligibility is proven, what happens to the record next, which kind of issue most constrains it, and how much time is left in the screening window.

eligibility_proven.instructions: Recorded evidence shows the subject meets every inclusion and exclusion criterion.

criteria.true: Every criterion supported by valid, in-window, reconciled source values
criteria.false: Any criterion unmet, unverified, contradicted or merely plausible

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this screening record next?

criteria.release: No open issue; record released for randomisation as it stands.
criteria.hold_query: One confirmable gap; randomisation waits on a single site response.
criteria.rescreen: Repeatable defect or lapsed window; a new screening visit is needed.
criteria.screen_fail: Criterion definitively unmet on valid data; subject is excluded.

primary_issue.instructions: Which single issue type most constrains this subject's eligibility?

criteria.no_issue: Sections reconcile; no documentation, clinical or timing problem found.
criteria.documentation: Consent, signature or identifier defect; outranks all other issue types.
criteria.clinical_value: Lab or medication conflicts with criterion; documentation sound, outranks timing.
criteria.timing_window: Only remaining problem is a date outside a protocol window.

affected_scope.instructions: How many people or units does this issue directly affect?
criteria: Affects one person or unit only
Affects two to five people or units
Affects six to twenty people or units
Affects more than twenty people or units

window_left.instructions: How many days remain before the screening window closes?
criteria: Window already closed on the review date
One to three days remain in window
Four to ten days remain in window
More than ten days remain in window

factors.name: lab_reconciliation
factors.description: How a key lab value in labs compares with the value transcribed into the matching eligibility criterion: identical; same value in a different unit that agrees after conversion; small transcription rounding not crossing the threshold; or a transcription that hides a threshold crossing

factors.name: consent_status
factors.description: State of informed consent: current version signed before any procedure; superseded version signed but re-consent on the current version also on file; superseded version only; or signature date later than the first screening procedure

factors.name: window_days_remaining
factors.description: Days between the review date and the window end, where window end is the consent date plus the protocol screening window length; negative means already closed

factors.name: collection_date_mismatch
factors.description: A lab collection date in labs differs from the visit date in visit; sometimes by one day within window, sometimes placing the sample before consent or outside the lab validity window

factors.name: prohibited_conmed
factors.description: A concomitant medication whose class matches the protocol's prohibited list appears in conmeds

factors.name: washout_completed
factors.description: Mitigation for a prohibited medication: its stop date precedes the visit date by at least the required washout days; sampled independently so the alarming medication appears with and without it about equally

factors.name: out_of_range_lab
factors.description: One protocol-relevant lab result falls outside the criterion threshold on first draw

factors.name: valid_repeat_on_file
factors.description: Mitigation for an out-of-range lab: a repeat sample within window and within the protocol's allowed repeat count is in range; sometimes the repeat exists but exceeds the allowed repeat count

factors.name: boundary_value
factors.description: A lab or age value sits exactly on a criterion threshold whose inequality direction is ambiguous between the criterion text code and the lab reference format, leaving judges split

factors.name: identifier_mismatch
factors.description: Subject identifiers disagree across sections: none; initials transposed on the consent record; or the screening number on a lab requisition differs from the subject section

factors.name: investigator_signoff
factors.description: Investigator eligibility sign-off: signed after all results; signed before the last lab result was dated; or unsigned

factors.name: open_query_count
factors.description: Number of unresolved data queries listed against the record; closed queries are also listed as decoys

sections.name: subject
sections.description: Screening number, initials, date of birth, sex, site code

sections.name: consent
sections.description: Form version signed, current approved version, signature dates, re-consent entries

sections.name: visit
sections.description: Visit date, review date, protocol window length, procedures with dates

sections.name: labs
sections.description: List of results with test code, value, unit, threshold, collection date, requisition number, repeat flag

sections.name: eligibility
sections.description: Criterion checks with recorded values and site met flags, investigator sign-off, query list

sections.name: conmeds
sections.description: Medications with class, start and stop dates, prohibited-class list and washout days

F302.rendering_notes: Each factor appears only through raw fields. lab_reconciliation: labs[].value and unit set against eligibility.criteria[].recorded_value and unit; unit_only uses umol/L versus mg/dL, or g/L versus g/dL. consent_status: consent.form_version versus consent.current_version, consent.signed_date versus the earliest visit.procedures[].date, and consent.reconsent[] entries. window_days_remaining: never shown; derived from consent.signed_date plus visit.window_days minus visit.review_date. collection_date_mismatch: labs[].collected versus visit.visit_date, consent.signed_date and labs[].valid_days. prohibited_conmed and washout_completed: conmeds.items[].class against conmeds.prohibited_classes, with items[].stop compared to visit.visit_date and washout_days; stop may be null, meaning ongoing. out_of_range_lab and valid_repeat_on_file: labs[] entries with repeat:true, with labs.max_repeats in the protocol block. boundary_value: a value equal to the threshold, where criteria[].operator is written as "lt" while labs[].threshold_format shows "<=". identifier_mismatch: subject.initials and screening_no versus consent.initials and labs[].requisition_screening_no. investigator_signoff: eligibility.signoff.signed (boolean) and signoff.date versus the latest labs[].collected. open_query_count: eligibility.queries[] with status open or closed. Decoys: site-entered criteria[].met flags are sometimes true despite a crossing, so they must not be trusted; labs[].flag H/L marks reference-range deviations that may be irrelevant to protocol thresholds; closed queries; superseded consent versions that were properly re-consented; prohibited-class medications stopped well before the visit. No field states eligibility, disposition, issue type, days remaining or affected scope. There is no overall status field and no free-text notes.

F303.role: Clinical service coordinator at a home oxygen supplier, reviewing each completed delivery and installation visit record before it is closed or followed up
F303.setting: A regional home oxygen service delivers concentrators, portable units and cylinders to patients' homes against an active prescription. Each visit produces a structured record covering the prescription and order, what the technician left and installed, the home fire-safety assessment, equipment fault history and the supply plan. The coordinator checks one visit record at a time. They decide whether the delivery matched the prescription, how far the order was fulfilled, how long on-site oxygen will last, how many safety hazards remain open, and what should happen to the record next.

rx_match.instructions: Delivered equipment matches the active prescription's modality and flow rate.

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this delivery record next?

criteria.close_record: No outstanding items, checks or paperwork; file as complete.
criteria.chase_paperwork: Only a signature or document is missing; no return visit.
criteria.hold_confirm: One fact needs phone confirmation before closing or rebooking.
criteria.book_revisit: Return visit needed for items or setup, not same-day.
criteria.urgent_dispatch: Same-day visit needed because supply or safety is critical.

fulfilment.instructions: How much of the ordered delivery was actually fulfilled on this visit?

criteria.nothing_delivered: No prescribed items were left on site during this visit.
criteria.items_short: Some items left, but at least one prescribed item missing.
criteria.setup_incomplete: All items left; install, testing or training not finished.
criteria.fully_complete: All items left and every install check logged complete.

supply_runway.instructions: How long will on-site oxygen last at prescribed usage?
criteria: Critical: under 12 hours at prescribed flow and hours
Short: 12 to 48 hours at prescribed usage
Adequate: over 48 hours, up to 7 days
Ample: over 7 days, or concentrator verified working

open_hazards.instructions: How many home safety hazards remain unresolved at visit close?
criteria: No unresolved hazards at visit close
Exactly one unresolved hazard at visit close
Two unresolved hazards at visit close
Three unresolved hazards at visit close
Four or more unresolved hazards at visit close

factors.name: rx_alignment
factors.description: How the delivered equipment relates to the active prescription: exact match, flow setting differs from prescribed flow, wrong modality (e.g. cylinders only where a concentrator is prescribed), or the prescription had expired before the visit date.

factors.name: items_shortfall
factors.description: Gap between items_ordered and items_left: none, one SKU short or under quantity, several SKUs short, or nothing left (no access or patient declined).

factors.name: setup_state
factors.description: Completion of installation checks: all logged, training not given, flow or alarm test not logged, or the install_checks object entirely null.

factors.name: supply_hours
factors.description: True hours of oxygen available on site at prescribed flow and daily hours, derived from cylinder sizes, fill levels and whether a working concentrator is installed; values cluster near the 12, 48 and 168 hour boundaries often.

factors.name: concentrator_fault
factors.description: Equipment fault log shows a concentrator fault code raised during or shortly before the visit (alarming signal).

factors.name: fault_mitigated
factors.description: When a fault is present, a later fault-log entry shows retest_passed true or a replacement serial was swapped in on the same visit; sampled independently so the fault appears with and without mitigation about equally.

factors.name: hazards_found
factors.description: Number of hazards recorded on the site assessment (smoker in household, open flame appliance, no smoke alarm, tubing trip risk, cylinder stored near heat).

factors.name: hazard_mitigation
factors.description: Whether hazards that were found were mostly resolved on the visit (fire-break valves fitted, cylinders relocated, alarm fitted); each recorded hazard carries status resolved_on_visit or open, so alarming hazard codes appear resolved about half the time.

factors.name: hazard_status_missing
factors.description: One recorded hazard has status null because it was not rechecked before departure, leaving the open-hazard count on a boundary.

factors.name: handover_gap
factors.description: Patient signature null or handover_at timestamp missing while everything else is complete; a paperwork-only gap.

factors.name: timeline_out_of_order
factors.description: install_checks.completed_at earlier than visit.arrived_at, or departed_at before arrived_at, casting doubt on whether checks really happened on this visit.

factors.name: next_delivery
factors.description: State of the next scheduled delivery relative to the supply runway: booked before supply runs out, booked after it runs out, or not booked; a timely booking mitigates short supply.

factors.name: dependency_level
factors.description: Prescribed usage pattern: ambulatory only, nocturnal, or continuous 24-hour use; changes how far a given cylinder stock lasts.

factors.name: billing_hold
factors.description: Decoy: account carries a billing hold or arrears flag that looks alarming but has no bearing on clinical supply, fulfilment or safety.

sections.name: order
sections.description: Order id, prescription (modality, flow_lpm, hours_per_day, rx_expiry), items_ordered list of sku and qty, and account flags.

sections.name: visit
sections.description: Visit id and date, arrived_at, departed_at, items_left list with sku, qty and serial, install_checks object, patient_signature, handover_at.

sections.name: site_assessment
sections.description: assessed_at timestamp and a hazards list, each with a hazard code, status and fix code.

sections.name: equipment
sections.description: Installed concentrator serial and flow_setting_lpm, fault_log entries, and cylinders_on_site with size code and fill_pct.

sections.name: supply_plan
sections.description: Next delivery date, delivery window and the route day assigned.

F303.rendering_notes: rx_alignment: compare order.prescription.modality and flow_lpm with visit.items_left SKUs and equipment.concentrator.flow_setting_lpm; rx_expired shows as order.prescription.rx_expiry earlier than visit.visit_date. Never include a match flag. items_shortfall: visible only by comparing order.items_ordered with visit.items_left; nothing_left gives an empty items_left list and access_achieved false. setup_state: visit.install_checks has booleans flow_verified, alarm_tested, training_given and a completed_at time; individual booleans are false or null, and checks_null makes the whole object null. supply_hours is never stated. It must be derived from equipment.cylinders_on_site (size codes such as CD 460 L, ZD 300 L, HX 2300 L with fill_pct), order.prescription.flow_lpm and hours_per_day (driven by dependency_level). A concentrator counts only if installed with no unresolved fault. concentrator_fault adds an equipment.fault_log entry with a code such as LOW_PURITY or HIGH_PRESSURE. fault_mitigated adds a later entry with retest_passed true, or a second concentrator serial in items_left. hazards_found and hazard_mitigation shape the site_assessment.hazards list; each entry has a status of open or resolved_on_visit and a fix code (firebreak_fitted, cylinder_relocated, alarm_fitted, or null). hazard_status_missing sets one status to null. handover_gap sets visit.patient_signature to null or omits handover_at. timeline_out_of_order puts install_checks.completed_at before visit.arrived_at, or makes departed_at precede arrived_at. next_delivery shows as supply_plan.next_delivery_date, or null if not_booked, and is compared against the derived runway. billing_hold appears as order.account.billing_hold true with an arrears_gbp amount; it is a decoy. Other decoys: customer satisfaction rating, technician id, route day, and prior visit count; none bear on the answers. No free-text fields. No field may state fulfilment status, urgency, risk level, hazard totals, supply hours or a recommended action.

F304.role: Non-emergency patient transport booking clerk in a hospital transport control office. The clerk checks each submitted journey booking against the patient's clinical and eligibility details before releasing it to dispatch.
F304.setting: An acute hospital trust runs its own non-emergency patient transport service for outpatient appointments, discharges, dialysis, chemotherapy and inter-site transfers. Wards and clinics submit bookings through an internal system. A control clerk reviews each booking one at a time before it goes to the dispatch board. The clerk checks the requested vehicle and crew against the latest mobility assessment and equipment needs. The clerk also checks eligibility and exemptions, the pickup window against the estimated journey time, and the ward, referrer and control notes. Records often carry conflicting values between sections, partial confirmations and reassuring details that may or may not settle a concern.

vehicle_fit.instructions: The booked vehicle class fits the patient's assessed mobility and equipment.

criteria.true: Vehicle class matches current assessment and listed equipment.
criteria.false: Vehicle mismatched, or assessment missing or out of date.

disposition.instructions: What should happen to this booking before dispatch?

criteria.confirm: No conflicts or outstanding items; dispatch exactly as submitted.
criteria.amend_confirm: Correctable field conflict, nothing outstanding; fix then dispatch.
criteria.hold: One confirmation outstanding from ward; dispatch not yet safe.
criteria.decline: Eligibility unmet with no recorded exception; refer elsewhere.

crew_config.instructions: Which crew configuration does this journey require?

criteria.single_crew: No oxygen or monitoring; patient walks or sits unaided.
criteria.double_crew: Wheelchair or stretcher transfer needed, without oxygen or monitoring.
criteria.clinical_escort: Oxygen or en-route monitoring needed, patient under bariatric limit.
criteria.specialist_team: Weight over bariatric limit or high-flow oxygen needing specialist kit.

time_pressure.instructions: How tight is the pickup window against required arrival time?
criteria: Over 90 minutes spare after estimated journey
30 to 90 minutes spare, inclusive
Under 30 minutes spare, arrival still on time
Estimated journey overruns window; arrival will be late

delay_impact.instructions: What clinical consequence follows if this journey runs late?
criteria: Low: routine outpatient slot, rebookable, no treatment involved
Moderate: discharge held, or treatment reslotted same day
High: treatment session lost, no same-day reslot available
Critical: theatre or transfer slot lost, no same-day alternative

factors.name: mobility_alignment
factors.description: How request.mobility_booked and request.vehicle_class compare with patient.mobility_assessed and its date. 'understated' means the booking asks for less than the assessment shows (seated for a stretcher patient). 'overstated' means it asks for more. 'stale' means the assessment is more than 30 days older than the journey. 'missing' means the assessment is null.

factors.name: secondary_discrepancy
factors.description: A second cross-section mismatch, placed in varied fields and never flagged. 'ward_trivial' is a pickup ward code in a different format but the same ward. 'address_material' is a request pickup that differs from the patient's current location. 'time_trivial' is an appointment time differing by 5 minutes or less between request and journey. 'time_material' is a difference of more than 20 minutes. 'equipment_unlisted' is equipment named in a note but absent from request.equipment.

factors.name: eligibility_concern
factors.description: Whether patient fields suggest the patient may not meet transport eligibility. Examples: own_transport_available true, mobility independent, or a note saying a relative usually drives.

factors.name: eligibility_exception
factors.description: Mitigation for an eligibility concern. An approved exemption code with approver and date is recorded in patient.exemption, for example a carer unable to assist a transfer or post-sedation travel. It appears with and without an eligibility concern about equally.

factors.name: clinical_support
factors.description: The highest en-route support the patient needs, shown through patient.oxygen_lpm, patient.monitoring and patient.weight_kg. Weight is compared with the service bariatric limit of 160 kg. The level of support determines the crew configuration, with the highest requirement taking precedence.

factors.name: crew_request_gap
factors.description: How request.crew_requested compares with the configuration that clinical_support implies. The request can be correct, one step too low or one step too high.

factors.name: buffer_minutes
factors.description: Required arrival time minus (latest pickup plus estimated journey duration), in minutes. Negative values mean a late arrival. The value is derived from journey.window_end, journey.est_duration_min and request.appt_time, and is never shown directly.

factors.name: duration_estimate_split
factors.description: Whether the journey section carries two duration estimates, a routing estimate and a control-room manual estimate. The two estimates straddle the 30-minute or 90-minute buffer threshold, leaving the time pressure level contestable.

factors.name: late_tolerance
factors.description: Mitigation for a tight window. The destination has recorded late-arrival tolerance in minutes (journey.late_tolerance_min greater than 0), or a note confirms the clinic will hold the slot. This changes the disposition but not the time pressure score. It appears near half the time regardless of buffer.

factors.name: appointment_type
factors.description: The purpose of the journey, given in request.appt_type with a matching destination department. This is the base input for the delay impact score.

factors.name: same_day_reslot
factors.description: Mitigation for delay impact. The receiving unit notes that it can reslot the patient the same day, shown as a note line or destination.reslot_same_day true. It lowers delay impact by one band for treatment and theatre journeys. It appears near half the time.

factors.name: confirmation_pending
factors.description: Exactly one item is outstanding before dispatch is safe. Examples: discharge medicines not yet ready, fit-to-travel sign-off blank, or the escort name to be confirmed. It appears as a null field plus a note line.

factors.name: prior_aborts
factors.description: The number of aborted journeys in the last 90 days in the history list. Each has a reason. Some reasons are unrelated and benign, such as clinic cancelled or a weather day. Others relate to the current booking, such as wrong vehicle sent or patient not ready.

factors.name: aborts_related
factors.description: Whether at least one prior abort reason matches a problem present in the current booking, such as wrong vehicle class or patient not ready. If false, any aborts present are decoys.

sections.name: request
sections.description: Booking as submitted: ref, requester, appt_type, appt_time, vehicle_class, crew_requested, mobility_booked, equipment list, pickup and destination codes.

sections.name: patient
sections.description: Patient details: pt_ref, mobility_assessed, assessed_on, weight_kg, oxygen_lpm, monitoring, own_transport_available, carer_available, exemption object or null, current_location.

sections.name: journey
sections.description: Planning data: window_start, window_end, est_duration_min, manual_est_min or null, distance_km, late_tolerance_min, destination.reslot_same_day.

sections.name: history
sections.description: List of prior journeys in the last 90 days, each with date, outcome (completed or aborted), vehicle_class and reason.

sections.name: notes
sections.description: One to three short free-text lines: ward_note, referrer_note, control_note, each a single sentence or null.

F304.rendering_notes: mobility_alignment: shown by comparing request.mobility_booked and request.vehicle_class with patient.mobility_assessed and patient.assessed_on against request.appt_time. A stale or null assessment makes vehicle_fit false even when the values agree. secondary_discrepancy: placed in the field pair it names. Trivial variants include a ward code written 'W12' against 'Ward 12', or a 3-minute time difference. These are decoys that do not justify amend_confirm on their own. Material variants (an address mismatch, a time difference over 20 minutes, unlisted equipment such as 'needs own oxygen cylinder' in ward_note while request.equipment omits it) do justify it. eligibility_concern: shown by own_transport_available true, mobility independent or a referrer_note remark. eligibility_exception: shown as patient.exemption {code, approved_by, approved_on}, or null when absent. A concern with no exception leads to decline. A concern with an exception does not. clinical_support: shown only through numbers and flags: oxygen_lpm 0 or null, 2, or 10 (10 counts as high flow), monitoring 'cardiac' or null, and weight_kg (decoy weights of 150 to 159 sit just under the 160 kg limit). crew_request_gap: request.crew_requested differs from the implied configuration without any comment. buffer_minutes: derived only from window_end, est_duration_min and appt_time. Never print a buffer or slack field. duration_estimate_split: when true, manual_est_min is non-null and moves the buffer across 30 or 90. late_tolerance: journey.late_tolerance_min greater than 0, or a control_note stating the clinic will hold the slot. same_day_reslot: destination.reslot_same_day true, or a note line; it is null or false otherwise. confirmation_pending: one null field (for example fit_to_travel_signed or escort_name) plus a matching note sentence; if any confirmation is pending, the disposition is hold rather than amend_confirm. prior_aborts and aborts_related: shown as history entries with outcome 'aborted' and a reason. Unrelated reasons are decoys that must not raise concern alone. Never include fields that state an answer: no priority, risk, eligible, approved_for_dispatch, crew_required or urgency fields, and notes never say what the clerk should decide. Status-like values a real system shows, such as an exemption code, are acceptable.

F305.role: Haemodialysis charge nurse doing end-of-shift sign-off of completed session logs
F305.setting: A hospital satellite haemodialysis unit. Each treatment produces a structured session log from the dialysis machine export, the chairside observation chart and the pre-treatment checklist. Before a log is closed, the charge nurse reviews it alone. The nurse reconciles delivered treatment against the prescription, confirms the safety checks and decides whether the log can be signed off, queried, referred or reported.

uf_reconciles.instructions: Machine fluid removal agrees with the recorded weight loss within 0.5 kg.

criteria.true: Both weights present; net UF within 0.5 kg of change.
criteria.false: Post weight missing, or the gap exceeds 0.5 kg.

checks_before_start.instructions: All mandatory pre-treatment checks were documented before the treatment start time.

log_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this session log at review?

criteria.sign_off: All sections reconcile; no open checks or clinical findings remain.
criteria.hold_query: One missing or inconsistent entry needs confirmation from the treating nurse.
criteria.refer_prescriber: Clinical finding needs nephrologist review before the patient's next session.
criteria.incident_report: Safety event or wrong setting delivered requires a formal incident report.

time_shortfall.instructions: How far did delivered treatment time fall short of prescription?
criteria: Full: effective time within 5 minutes of prescribed
Minor: effective time short by 6 to 15 minutes
Moderate: effective time short by 16 to 30 minutes
Major: effective time short by over 30 minutes

pending_age.instructions: How long has this record been waiting without any decision?
criteria: Logged less than 24 hours ago
Waiting between one and seven days
Waiting between eight and thirty days
Waiting more than thirty days without decision

factors.name: time_shortfall_min
factors.description: Minutes by which effective treatment time (needling-on to washback, minus machine pauses) falls short of the prescribed duration. Values cluster near the 5, 15 and 30-minute boundaries.

factors.name: machine_pause_min
factors.description: Total minutes the blood pump was stopped, recorded only as paired stop/resume entries in the machine alarm list and not deducted anywhere else.

factors.name: uf_weight_gap_kg
factors.description: Absolute gap between net machine UF (UF removed minus saline boluses and washback) and pre-weight minus post-weight. Values often sit near the 0.5 kg line.

factors.name: post_weight_missing
factors.description: Post-treatment weight not recorded, so fluid removal cannot be verified.

factors.name: missing_check
factors.description: Which mandatory pre-treatment check, if any, has no entry at all.

factors.name: check_logged_after_start
factors.description: A check is present but its timestamp falls after the treatment start time, showing it was done out of order or back-filled.

factors.name: prescription_mismatch
factors.description: Which machine setting, if any, differs from the prescription section.

factors.name: mismatch_magnitude
factors.description: Size of any setting mismatch. Trivial means rounding-level, such as blood flow 10 ml/min off or heparin 100 units off. Relevant means a different dialysate potassium bath, blood flow off by 50+ ml/min, or a different dialyser.

factors.name: hypotension_episodes
factors.description: Count of chairside systolic readings below 90 mmHg in the observation list.

factors.name: hypotension_mitigated
factors.description: A saline bolus and a UF-rate reduction are logged after the low reading, and the next systolic reading has recovered above 100 mmHg.

factors.name: circuit_clotted
factors.description: The extracorporeal circuit clotted and a line or dialyser change was logged, with blood loss not returned.

factors.name: prior_short_sessions
factors.description: Number of the last six sessions in history with effective time short by more than 15 minutes.

factors.name: documented_flow_reduction
factors.description: Decoy: blood flow was reduced mid-session with a coded access-pressure reason. It looks like a prescription mismatch but is an accepted adjustment.

sections.name: session
sections.description: Session id, patient ref, chair, date, needle_on and washback timestamps, nurse ids.

sections.name: prescription
sections.description: Prescribed duration_min, dialyser, dialysate_k and _ca, qb_ml_min, heparin_units, target_uf_ml, dry_weight_kg.

sections.name: machine
sections.description: Delivered settings, uf_removed_ml, washback_ml, and alarms list of coded events with timestamps.

sections.name: observations
sections.description: pre_kg, post_kg, list of bp readings with times, interventions list such as saline_bolus_ml.

sections.name: checks
sections.description: Pre-treatment checklist entries: check code, done boolean, timestamp, checker ids.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Last six sessions: date, prescribed_min, effective_min, post_kg.

F305.rendering_notes: time_shortfall_min is never stated. The reviewer derives effective time from session.needle_on and session.washback minus paired PUMP_STOP/PUMP_RESUME entries in machine.alarms (machine_pause_min), then compares it with prescription.duration_min. Clock duration alone is a decoy whenever pauses exist. uf_weight_gap_kg is rendered through machine.uf_removed_ml, machine.washback_ml, observations.interventions saline_bolus_ml, observations.pre_kg and observations.post_kg. When post_weight_missing applies, post_kg is null. missing_check omits that entry from the checks list entirely. check_logged_after_start gives one check a timestamp later than session.needle_on, with done true. prescription_mismatch shows as a machine.settings value differing from the matching prescription field, at the magnitude set by mismatch_magnitude. documented_flow_reduction adds an alarm QB_REDUCED with code ART_PRESSURE_HIGH and a lower machine.qb_actual. This differs from the prescription but is acceptable and must not count as a mismatch. Hypotension shows only as bp readings below 90 systolic; mitigation shows as an interventions entry plus the next reading. circuit_clotted shows as a CIRCUIT_CLOT alarm, a LINE_CHANGE event and an increased blood_loss_ml. prior_short_sessions lives only in the history list. For disposition, take the highest applicable option. A wrong relevant setting or an unreturned clot is an incident. Unmitigated hypotension, repeated short sessions or major shortfall are referrals. A single missing value or check is a hold. No field may state a status, shortfall, risk, verdict or summary flag, and there are no free-text fields; only codes, numbers, booleans, timestamps and nulls.

F306.role: Educational Visits Coordinator at a secondary school, reviewing each submitted trip risk assessment before sign-off
F306.setting: Teachers submit risk assessments for off-site trips through the school's visits management system. The coordinator opens one submission at a time and checks it across its sections: trip details, the pupil roster with consents and medical flags, the staff list, the planned activities with provider details, and the approvals log. Mismatches between sections are common and never announced. Alarming gaps often come with mitigating entries elsewhere in the record. The coordinator must decide whether consent and staffing hold up, how many unresolved inconsistencies remain, how well medical needs are covered, and what to do with the submission now.

consent_complete.instructions: Every rostered pupil has valid parental consent recorded or formally excepted.

staffing_adequate.instructions: Confirmed adults meet the required supervision ratio on every trip day.

criteria.true: Confirmed adult count meets ratio on all days.
criteria.false: Ratio short on any day, or adults unconfirmed.

disposition.instructions: What should the coordinator do with this submission now?

criteria.approve: No outstanding issues; trip proceeds exactly as submitted.
criteria.approve_conditions: Minor fixable issues; proceeds once organiser makes named changes.
criteria.hold: Exactly one pending external confirmation blocks decision until received.
criteria.return_revise: Multiple substantive gaps; organiser must rework and resubmit plan.
criteria.decline: Hazard or staffing gap unfixable before departure; trip cancelled.

mismatch_count.instructions: How many unresolved mismatches exist between sections of this record?
criteria: No unresolved mismatches between any sections
Exactly one unresolved mismatch between sections
Two or three unresolved mismatches between sections
Four or more unresolved mismatches between sections

medical_coverage.instructions: What share of medically flagged pupils have a care plan on file?
criteria: Absent: two or more flagged pupils, none with plans
Sparse: some plans held, under half of flagged covered
Partial: half or more covered, two or more lacking
Near: exactly one flagged pupil lacks a plan
Complete: every flagged pupil covered, or none flagged

factors.name: trip_type
factors.description: Kind of trip, which sets the required pupil-to-adult ratio and number of trip days.

factors.name: pupil_count
factors.description: Number of pupils on the roster; drives the staffing requirement and is restated in trip and transport fields.

factors.name: consent_gap
factors.description: State of parental consent across the roster: all valid, one missing, one expired before the trip date, or several missing.

factors.name: consent_exception_logged
factors.description: Whether the approvals log holds a head-approved consent exception covering the gap pupils (e.g. recorded verbal consent). Only matters when a gap exists; covers one gap pupil, never several.

factors.name: staffing_position
factors.description: Confirmed adults against the ratio requirement: surplus, exactly at ratio, one short on one day only, or one short on all days.

factors.name: provider_instructors_confirmed
factors.description: Whether the activity provider's contract entry confirms supervising instructors who may count toward the ratio for their sessions, closing a shortfall on those days.

factors.name: planted_mismatches
factors.description: Number of cross-section inconsistencies planted: headcount vs roster length, coach seats vs party size, staff attendance dates vs trip dates, return date vs accommodation nights, activity date outside trip window.

factors.name: amendment_explains_one
factors.description: Whether a logged, approved amendment explains one of the planted mismatches (e.g. a date change or late roster addition), so it is not unresolved.

factors.name: medical_flagged
factors.description: Number of pupils carrying a medical flag on the roster.

factors.name: plans_missing
factors.description: Number of flagged pupils with no care plan in the roster medical list, capped at medical_flagged.

factors.name: provider_holds_plan_copy
factors.description: Whether the provider record lists receipt of care plan copies for one of the missing-plan pupils, which counts as a plan on file.

factors.name: high_hazard_activity
factors.description: Licence position of the highest-tier activity: no high-tier activity, licence valid, licence expired with renewal pending, or licence missing.

factors.name: days_to_departure
factors.description: Days between the review date and departure; short lead times push unresolved gaps from conditions or hold toward revise or decline.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether one value is placed exactly on a threshold: consent expiring on departure day, adult count exactly at ratio with one adult joining on day two, or exactly half of flagged pupils covered.

sections.name: trip
sections.description: Trip id, destination, trip_type, depart/return dates, pupil_headcount, transport with seat count.

sections.name: roster
sections.description: Pupil list with id, year_group, consent_date, consent_expiry, medical_flag, care_plan_ref.

sections.name: staffing
sections.description: Adults with role, dbs_status, first_aid, confirmed flag and attend_from/attend_to dates.

sections.name: activities
sections.description: Planned activities with date, hazard_tier, provider id, licence_ref, licence_expiry, instructors_supplied, plan_copies_received.

sections.name: approvals
sections.description: Review date, ratio_required, amendments log, policy exceptions, prior visit reviews history.

F306.rendering_notes: trip_type appears as trip.trip_type; approvals.ratio_required is shown as a number (e.g. 10 meaning 1:10) and differs by type. pupil_count is the length of roster; trip.pupil_headcount and trip.transport.seats restate it and are where headcount mismatches are planted. consent_gap shows as roster entries with consent_date null (missing) or consent_expiry before trip.depart_date (expired); consent_exception_logged appears as an approvals.exceptions entry with type 'consent', pupil_id and approved_by, and covers only one pupil. staffing_position is derived only by comparing staffing entries with confirmed=true and attend_from/attend_to covering each trip day against roster length divided by ratio_required; unconfirmed adults are decoys that inflate the raw list. provider_instructors_confirmed appears as activities[].instructors_supplied > 0 with a provider contract_status 'signed'; instructors count only on that activity's date. planted_mismatches are scattered across trip, staffing dates, accommodation nights and activity dates; amendment_explains_one appears as an approvals.amendments entry whose field and new value match one mismatch. medical_flagged is the count of roster entries with medical_flag true; plans_missing is those with care_plan_ref null; provider_holds_plan_copy appears as a pupil id listed in activities[].plan_copies_received. high_hazard_activity shows via hazard_tier 3 with licence_ref present and licence_expiry after trip, expired with approvals.exceptions entry type 'licence_renewal' status 'pending', or licence_ref null. days_to_departure is depart_date minus approvals.review_date. Decoys: approvals.prior_reviews history (past trips passed or had incidents) and dbs_status 'renewal_due' for an adult with a valid date, neither of which change answers. No field states consent completeness, ratio met, mismatch count, coverage share, overall risk or a recommended disposition; the organiser's own self-rating is never included. Use null for unknown values, ISO dates, numbers as numbers, no free-text fields.

F307.role: Departmental chemical safety officer reviewing individual container records from routine lab inventory checks
F307.setting: A university chemistry department runs rolling inventory checks across research labs. Each record covers one chemical container at one check. It holds the registered stock entry, where the container was found, what the checker counted and observed, who is responsible for it, and its prior check history. The record also carries short notes from the checker and the custodian. The safety officer reviews each record on its own. They decide whether stock reconciles, whether storage is permitted, what happens next and how overdue the container's review is.

qty_reconciled.instructions: Found quantity reconciles with recorded quantity once logged usage is counted.

criteria.true: Gap after logged usage is 10% or less
criteria.false: Unexplained gap above 10%, or no count recorded

storage_permitted.instructions: Container's storage is permitted by class or a current approved exception.

criteria.true: Store type matches class, or exception unexpired at check
criteria.false: Wrong store type and no unexpired exception

next_action.instructions: What should happen with this container after the check?

criteria.sign_off: No defects found, or every finding already resolved and documented.
criteria.recheck_hold: Exactly one outstanding confirmation from custodian needed before closing.
criteria.corrective_task: Fixable defect needs custodian action; container stays in use meanwhile.
criteria.quarantine_dispose: Container unsafe or unaccounted for; withdraw from use immediately.

source_support.instructions: How many independent sources confirm the information in this record?
criteria: No independent source confirms the information
Exactly one independent source confirms it
Two or three independent sources confirm it
Four or more independent sources confirm it

review_overdue.instructions: How far past its review-by date is the container at check?
criteria: Review-by date not yet reached at check
Overdue by 1 to 29 days
Overdue by 30 to 180 days
Overdue by more than 180 days

factors.name: qty_discrepancy_pct
factors.description: Percentage gap between recorded quantity and found quantity before any logged usage is deducted

factors.name: usage_logged
factors.description: Whether usage withdrawals since the last check are logged and explain most of the gap

factors.name: qty_found_missing
factors.description: Checker left the found quantity null, so reconciliation cannot be shown

factors.name: store_mismatch
factors.description: Whether the store type where the container was found differs from the type its hazard class requires

factors.name: exception_status
factors.description: State of any approved storage exception covering the container at check date

factors.name: days_overdue
factors.description: Days between the container's review-by date and the check date; negative means not yet due

factors.name: recent_retest_passed
factors.description: For overdue items, whether a retest (peroxide strip or purity check) was logged after the due date with a passing result

factors.name: container_condition
factors.description: Physical state observed by the checker

factors.name: custodian_status
factors.description: Whether the named custodian is still in post or has left, with or without reassignment

factors.name: check_sequence_anomaly
factors.description: Check date earlier than the latest history entry, or the required photo missing while the checker's own text says one was taken

factors.name: prior_open_actions
factors.description: Count of unresolved actions from earlier checks on this container

factors.name: checker_note_tone
factors.description: Content of the checker's free-text note: absent, routine, alarming but resolved on the spot, or alarming and unresolved

factors.name: custodian_reply_pending_fix
factors.description: Custodian reply promises a single fix or confirmation not yet evidenced in the record

sections.name: container
sections.description: Registered stock entry: id, chem_name, cas_no, hazard_class, qty_recorded, unit, opened_on, review_by, peroxide_former

sections.name: location
sections.description: Where it was found: building, room, store_found, store_required, neighbours list of hazard classes

sections.name: check
sections.description: This check: checked_on, checker_id, qty_found, usage_since_last list, condition, label_legible, photo_attached, retest object or null

sections.name: owner
sections.description: Responsibility: pi_group, custodian, custodian_left_on, successor, exception object or null

sections.name: history
sections.description: List of prior checks with date, finding and action_status

sections.name: notes
sections.description: Free text: checker_note and custodian_reply, each one or two sentences or null

F307.rendering_notes: qty_discrepancy_pct is shown only indirectly as container.qty_recorded against check.qty_found (null when qty_found_missing). usage_logged appears as check.usage_since_last entries {date, qty, user} whose sum closes most of the gap when true; when false the list is empty or covers a small part. store_mismatch shows as location.store_found differing from location.store_required. exception_status is rendered as owner.exception null (none) or {ref, approved_by, expires}, with expires after checked_on (current) or before it (expired). The reviewer must compare dates. days_overdue is computed only from container.review_by against check.checked_on; never state the day count. recent_retest_passed appears as check.retest {date, method, result_ppm or result, pass}, dated after review_by; it lowers concern for next_action but does not change review_overdue. container_condition maps to check.condition and check.label_legible (worn_label sets it false). custodian_status shows via owner.custodian_left_on (null if active) and owner.successor (null when no successor). check_sequence_anomaly shows as checked_on earlier than the last history date, or photo_attached false while checker_note mentions a photo. prior_open_actions is the count of history entries with action_status 'open'. checker_note_tone and custodian_reply_pending_fix fill notes.checker_note and notes.custodian_reply; replies promise e.g. moving the bottle or recounting, without proof. Decoys: location.neighbours sometimes lists incompatible classes even when the store type is correct. Alarming words ('crusty cap', 'smells') sometimes appear in notes that also say the issue was cleaned or replaced. Peroxide_former true appears on items that are not overdue. Old closed history findings repeat past problems. No field may state a verdict: no 'reconciled', 'compliant', 'risk', 'overdue_days' or 'recommended_action' fields. Dates are ISO, quantities numeric with a separate unit, and unknowns are null.

F308.role: Exams officer reviewing access arrangement applications for a secondary school and sixth-form centre
F308.setting: Before each exam series, the exams officer reviews one candidate's access arrangement application at a time. Arrangements include extra time, a reader, a scribe, a word processor and rest breaks. The officer checks the request against the specialist assessment, the candidate's exam entries, the centre's register of approved assessors and the record of the candidate's normal way of working in internal tests. They then decide whether the application can be submitted to the awarding body, and in what form.

normal_working.instructions: Requested arrangements reflect the candidate's established normal way of working.

criteria.true: Usage log or recent onset supports each arrangement
criteria.false: Some arrangement lacks usage or valid recent-onset reason

assessor_valid.instructions: The assessment was conducted by an assessor on the centre register.

criteria.true: Assessor identifier matches an active register entry
criteria.false: Identifier absent, unmatched or registration lapsed then

disposition.instructions: How far can this application proceed towards submission?

criteria.decline: Evidence contradicts need or candidate is ineligible for arrangements
criteria.refer_reassess: Assessment invalid or expired; new specialist assessment required first
criteria.hold: Single confirmation outstanding, such as signature or identity correction
criteria.approve_reduced: Evidence supports some arrangements or a lower extra-time percentage
criteria.approve_full: Every requested arrangement fully supported and records reconcile

time_pressure.instructions: How soon is the candidate's first affected exam?
criteria: Routine: first affected exam more than 60 days away
Planned: first affected exam 31 to 60 days away
Pressing: first affected exam 8 to 30 days away
Critical: first affected exam within 7 days

unsupported_items.instructions: How many requested arrangements lack matching current supporting evidence?
criteria: Every requested arrangement matched by current evidence
Exactly one arrangement unsupported or only partly supported
Exactly two arrangements unsupported or partly supported
Three or more arrangements lack supporting evidence

factors.name: arrangement_count
factors.description: Number of distinct arrangements listed in the request

factors.name: extra_time_gap
factors.description: Requested extra-time percentage compared with the percentage the assessment recommends

factors.name: low_score_count
factors.description: Number of standardised scores below 85 in the assessment results that underpin the arrangements; some records hold a score of exactly 85

factors.name: assessment_window
factors.description: Assessment date relative to the start of the candidate's course of study

factors.name: assessor_registered
factors.description: Assessor identifier on the evidence appears in the centre register with active dates covering the assessment date

factors.name: usage_level
factors.description: Count of internal tests in the usage log where each requested arrangement was actually used

factors.name: recent_onset
factors.description: Need arose recently (new diagnosis or injury), so no usage history is expected; shown by onset date and arrangement type

factors.name: identity_mismatch
factors.description: Discrepancy between candidate details in the candidate section and in the evidence section

factors.name: consent_missing
factors.description: Candidate data-sharing consent not yet signed

factors.name: entry_scope_mismatch
factors.description: Request lists papers or subjects that do not appear in the candidate's exam entries

factors.name: days_to_first_exam
factors.description: Days from review date to the earliest entered exam that the request covers

factors.name: prior_decline
factors.description: A previous application for this candidate was declined

factors.name: prior_decline_superseded
factors.description: A newer assessment dated after the prior decline exists, removing the decline's relevance

sections.name: candidate
sections.description: Candidate number, name, date of birth, year group, course start date

sections.name: request
sections.description: List of requested arrangements with type, extra_time_pct, papers covered, consent_signed, onset_date

sections.name: evidence
sections.description: Assessment record: assessor_id, assessed_on, candidate name and DOB as recorded, standardised scores, recommended arrangements

sections.name: centre
sections.description: Registered assessors list with ids and active_from/active_to dates, review_date, prior application outcomes

sections.name: usage_history
sections.description: Internal tests list with date, subject and arrangements actually used

sections.name: entries
sections.description: Entered exams with paper code, subject and scheduled date

F308.rendering_notes: arrangement_count sets the length of request.arrangements. extra_time_gap appears as request.arrangements[].extra_time_pct compared against evidence.recommended[].extra_time_pct (bands 25, 50). low_score_count appears as evidence.scores[] with test name and standard_score; scores of exactly 85 sit on the boundary. assessment_window is evident only by comparing evidence.assessed_on with candidate.course_start. assessor_registered is evident only by matching evidence.assessor_id against centre.assessors[] and their active dates; unregistered cases show either a non-matching id or a lapsed active_to date. usage_level appears as how many usage_history.tests[] list each arrangement in arrangements_used. recent_onset sets request.onset_date within about 8 weeks of review_date, sometimes with a temporary arrangement type such as scribe_injury. identity_mismatch places a differing name, DOB or candidate number in evidence versus candidate. consent_missing sets request.consent_signed false or null. entry_scope_mismatch lists a paper code in request papers_covered that is absent from entries. days_to_first_exam is derived from centre.review_date against the earliest matching entries date. prior_decline appears in centre.prior_applications[] with outcome declined and a date; prior_decline_superseded puts evidence.assessed_on after that date. Decoys: a prior decline that has been superseded; low usage paired with a recent onset; name spelling differences such as hyphenation; unused rest-break columns; entries for unrelated subjects with near dates. No field states validity, eligibility, urgency, support counts or a recommended decision. Do not include free-text fields.

F309.role: Reading room duty supervisor in a rare books and special collections library, reviewing each advance consultation request before items are paged
F309.setting: Readers book a consultation slot and list the items they wish to see. Before anything is fetched, the duty supervisor opens the request record, which pulls together the reader's registration, the request as submitted, the catalogue records of the items, conservation survey data, the reader's visit history and any permissions or clearances. The supervisor then decides whether and how the request can go ahead. Records often contain small disagreements between sections, steps not yet done, and alarming flags that come with offsetting evidence.

reg_valid.instructions: Reader's registration is valid and verified on the consultation date.

disposition.instructions: What should the supervisor do with this request now?

criteria.approve: All checks pass; produce items as requested without added terms.
criteria.approve_conditions: Checks pass, but production requires stated handling or supervision terms.
criteria.hold: Exactly one confirmation is outstanding; keep the request pending until it arrives.
criteria.decline: A blocking failure exists, so the request cannot proceed this visit.

access_form.instructions: Under what arrangement should the most vulnerable requested item be consulted?

criteria.standard_table: Original used at an ordinary table without supports or invigilation.
criteria.supported: Original needs cradle, snake weights or foam, but no invigilation.
criteria.invigilated_table: Original used only at the supervised table under staff watch.
criteria.surrogate_only: Original withheld; reader uses the digital or microfilm copy.
criteria.not_produced: Neither original nor any surrogate can be offered this visit.

items_blocked.instructions: How many requested items cannot be produced as requested?
criteria: None: all requested items producible as catalogued and asked.
One: exactly one item blocked, substituted or deferred.
Several: two or more items affected, but not all.
All: no requested item can be produced as asked.

handling_risk.instructions: How high is the handling risk of the most vulnerable item?
criteria: Worst item graded good, with no fragility flags.
Worst item fair, or fragile with treatment logged after survey.
Worst item fragile, with no treatment logged since survey.
Worst item graded poor or under an active conservation hold.

factors.name: reg_validity
factors.description: State of the reader's registration relative to the requested slot: current and verified, expiring between submission and slot, already lapsed at submission, or present but photo ID never verified.

factors.name: renewal_pending
factors.description: Whether a registration renewal has been submitted but not yet processed; mitigates an expiry and makes hold the natural disposition rather than decline.

factors.name: item_count
factors.description: Number of items listed in the request.

factors.name: shelfmark_mismatch
factors.description: How the shelfmark or volume the reader typed differs from the catalogue record it was matched to: no difference, a trivial formatting difference, a different volume of the same work, or a different item altogether.

factors.name: worst_condition
factors.description: Condition grade of the most vulnerable requested item from the latest conservation survey.

factors.name: treated_since_survey
factors.description: Whether conservation treatment was completed on the worst item after its survey date, lowering effective risk; the date must be compared with the survey date and may sit before it as a decoy.

factors.name: conservation_hold
factors.description: Conservation hold state on any requested item: none, active hold, or hold placed and later lifted with a release date.

factors.name: surrogate_available
factors.description: Whether a digital or microfilm surrogate exists for the most vulnerable or blocked item.

factors.name: offsite_unretrieved
factors.description: Number of requested items held at the off-site store whose retrieval is not yet logged as complete.

factors.name: lead_days
factors.description: Working days between submission and slot; off-site retrieval needs three working days, so a short lead with unretrieved items blocks those items unless a courier is booked.

factors.name: restricted_permission
factors.description: Whether any item is under depositor restriction and the state of its permission: unrestricted, permission granted, permission requested but pending, or restriction with no permission record at all.

factors.name: prior_incident
factors.description: Most significant prior handling incident in the reader's visit history.

factors.name: incident_cleared
factors.description: Whether a supervisor clearance for the reader exists, dated after the latest incident; mitigates recent or serious incidents so that conditions rather than decline apply.

factors.name: sequence_anomaly
factors.description: Whether a date shows a step out of order, such as permission granted dated after the slot, ID verification dated after the first paging, or clearance dated before the incident it supposedly clears.

sections.name: reader
sections.description: Registration record: reader_id, category, reg_issued, reg_expiry, id_verified, id_verified_on, renewal_submitted_on.

sections.name: request
sections.description: Request as submitted: request_id, reader_id, submitted_on, slot_date, slot_session, and a list of items with shelfmark_as_typed and vol_as_typed.

sections.name: items
sections.description: Catalogue records matched to each request line: shelfmark, vol, record_id, location, retrieval_status, retrieved_on, courier_booked, restriction, surrogate_type.

sections.name: conservation
sections.description: Per-shelfmark survey data: condition_grade, survey_date, fragility_flags list, treatment_completed_on, hold_placed_on, hold_released_on, supports_required.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Reader's visit history: visits_total, last_visit, and an incidents list with date and grade.

sections.name: approvals
sections.description: Permissions and clearances: depositor_permission entries with requested_on, granted_on, and supervisor_clearance with cleared_on, scope.

F309.rendering_notes: reg_validity shows only through reader.reg_expiry compared with request.slot_date and request.submitted_on, and through id_verified (false or null with id_verified_on null for id_unverified); renewal_pending appears as reader.renewal_submitted_on with a date or null. Shelfmark mismatch is never flagged: compare request.items[].shelfmark_as_typed and vol_as_typed with items[].shelfmark and vol (format_only differs in spacing, case or punctuation only; volume_differs changes vol; different_item changes the shelfmark number). worst_condition appears in conservation[].condition_grade, with fragility_flags such as loose_boards or red_rot; treated_since_survey is treatment_completed_on later than survey_date, while a decoy treatment date earlier than the survey appears on some untreated records. conservation_hold is hold_placed_on with hold_released_on null (active) or a date (lifted). surrogate_available is items[].surrogate_type set to digital or microfilm, or null. offsite_unretrieved shows as items with location offsite and retrieval_status requested or null rather than on_reserve; lead_days is derived from submitted_on and slot_date, and courier_booked true can mitigate a short lead. restricted_permission shows as items[].restriction depositor plus an approvals.depositor_permission entry with granted_on set (granted), granted_on null (pending) or no entry at all (no_record). prior_incident appears in history.incidents with date and grade minor or serious; incident_cleared is approvals.supervisor_clearance.cleared_on later than the latest incident. sequence_anomaly is a date placed out of order in one of these fields. Decoys: reader.category, history.visits_total, items[].record_id, a format_only shelfmark difference, supports_required on items whose grade is good, and an expired lapsed registration from a previous year in reg_issued. No field states a disposition, risk level, access arrangement, count of blocked items or validity verdict; there is no status, risk or recommendation field, and no free-text notes.

F310.role: Benefits reassessment officer reviewing one claimant's periodic eligibility reassessment for a means-tested housing and living-costs support award
F310.setting: A regional welfare office runs scheduled reassessments of existing awards. Each record brings together the claimant's current award, their latest declaration, figures verified from external data feeds, the case history and a short officer or caseworker note. The officer must decide whether circumstances have changed without being reported, what to do with the award now, what kind of change matters most, and how long payments may have been affected.

undeclared_change.instructions: Verified data shows an unreported change that alters the entitlement band.

criteria.true: Trusted verified figure contradicts declaration and crosses band threshold.
criteria.false: No contradiction, change reported, explained, or below threshold.

next_step.instructions: What should the officer do with this reassessment now?

criteria.continue_award: Entitlement confirmed; current award continues at the same rate.
criteria.hold_pending: One outstanding item must be confirmed before any decision.
criteria.revise_award: Entitlement stands but the award rate must be recalculated.
criteria.suspend_payment: Payments stop while apparent nil entitlement is formally investigated.

change_category.instructions: Which type of change most affects entitlement on this record?

criteria.no_change: No verified change that would move the entitlement calculation.
criteria.income_change: Earnings, pension or other income differs from assessed figures.
criteria.household_change: A person has joined or left the assessed household.
criteria.housing_cost_change: Rent, tenancy terms or address differ from assessed figures.

affected_scope.instructions: How many people or units does this issue directly affect?
criteria: Affects one person or unit only
Affects two to five people or units
Affects six to twenty people or units
Affects more than twenty people or units

affected_duration.instructions: How long have payments potentially been affected by the change?
criteria: No affected payment period identified in the record
Affected period shorter than 4 weeks
Affected period from 4 to 26 weeks
Affected period longer than 26 weeks

factors.name: change_type
factors.description: The true kind of circumstance change underlying the record, if any; determines which section pair carries the contradiction.

factors.name: discrepancy_size
factors.description: Size of the gap between the declared and verified value relative to the award band threshold: trivial stays well inside the band, moderate moves the rate, large removes entitlement.

factors.name: discrepancy_location
factors.description: Which pair of sections must be compared to find the mismatch: declared earnings vs payroll feed, declared savings vs bank snapshot, household list vs tenancy occupants, or a term in the case note vs the listed household.

factors.name: change_reported
factors.description: Whether the claimant reported the change through a contact log entry dated before the reassessment, mitigating an apparent contradiction.

factors.name: benign_explanation
factors.description: Whether a field explains the alarming figure innocently, such as a one-off backdated pay correction, a temporary visitor flag, or an approved rent-arrears arrangement.

factors.name: weeks_since_change
factors.description: Weeks between the verified effective date of the change and the reassessment date; drives the affected-period answer.

factors.name: pending_evidence
factors.description: Whether one requested document (payslip, tenancy agreement, departure confirmation) is still outstanding in history requests.

factors.name: data_source_trust
factors.description: Origin of the contradicting figure: an automated verified feed, a claimant upload, or an unverified third-party report; lower trust weakens the contradiction.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether a key value sits exactly on a scale or band edge, such as the verified income equal to the taper threshold or the change dated exactly 4 or 26 weeks back.

factors.name: prior_overpayments
factors.description: Count of earlier overpayment episodes in history; a decoy that looks alarming but does not decide the current record.

factors.name: note_tone
factors.description: Tone of the free-text case note: neutral, alarming (suspicion voiced without evidence) or reassuring (unsupported comfort); decoy unless it names a concrete fact.

factors.name: recalculation_started
factors.description: Whether a recalculation was begun but not completed, shown by a draft rate in the award section with no approval date.

sections.name: award
sections.description: Current award: reference, weekly_rate, band, band thresholds, last_assessed date, draft_rate and draft_approved_on.

sections.name: declaration
sections.description: Claimant's latest declared figures: monthly earnings, savings, household members, rent, address, declared_on.

sections.name: verified_data
sections.description: Externally sourced figures with source, retrieved_on, effective_from, and one evidence_line free-text field.

sections.name: household
sections.description: Listed occupants with relationship, date joined, date left, temporary flag, plus tenancy occupant count.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Dated list of contact log entries, evidence requests with status, and prior overpayment episodes.

sections.name: case_notes
sections.description: Reassessment date, officer initials and one short free-text note.

F310.rendering_notes: change_type and discrepancy_location decide where the contradiction lives: income shows as declaration.monthly_earnings vs verified_data.payroll_monthly (or declaration.savings vs verified_data.bank_balance); household shows as household.members vs household.tenancy_occupants or a name/relative mentioned in case_notes.note that is absent from the members list; housing_costs shows as declaration.rent or address vs verified_data.landlord_rent or address. discrepancy_size is rendered only as raw numbers; the reader must compare the gap with award.band_lower/band_upper and taper_threshold. weeks_since_change is rendered as verified_data.effective_from against case_notes.reassessment_date; never print a weeks count. change_reported appears as a history contact entry (type 'change_notified', dated, short message) or its absence. benign_explanation appears as a field such as verified_data.one_off_payment=true, household member temporary=true with an end date, or an evidence_line like 'Includes backdated arrears correction for March'. data_source_trust is verified_data.source. pending_evidence is a history request with status 'outstanding'. recalculation_started is award.draft_rate non-null with draft_approved_on null. boundary_case places a value exactly at a threshold or a date exactly 28 or 182 days back. Decoys: prior_overpayments in history, note_tone in case_notes.note, unchanged fields that look large (e.g. high rent that matches both sections), and trivial mismatches such as rounding or a postcode spacing difference. Use null for unknown values. The record must never contain fields like 'change_detected', 'recommended_action', 'overpayment_weeks' or 'risk'; answers must be inferred by comparing sections.

F311.role: Verification supervisor at a constituency count centre, reviewing each polling station's closing report as its ballot box is received and verified
F311.setting: On election night each polling station sends its sealed ballot box with a closing report: station details, a timeline of close and transport, the presiding officer's ballot paper account, seal and packet records, and the count centre's own verification figures. The supervisor checks one report at a time and decides whether custody held, what kind of figure problem exists, how large any unexplained gap is, how much required paperwork is missing, and what to do with the box before it joins the count.

custody_unbroken.instructions: Ballot box custody was unbroken from close of poll to verification.

box_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this box before it joins the count?

criteria.accept: Figures reconcile, custody intact and paperwork complete; send to count.
criteria.accept_noted: Only minor explained or clerical issues; accept and log note.
criteria.hold_query: One missing item or fact needs presiding officer confirmation first.
criteria.recount_box: Unexplained gap in figures requires the box to be re-verified.
criteria.refer_ro: Custody break or seal doubt needs the returning officer's decision.

figure_problem.instructions: What is the most serious figure problem in this report?

criteria.none: Account lines, totals and verified count all agree exactly.
