criteria.arithmetic_slip: Account lines mis-summed or mis-copied, but papers physically reconcile.
criteria.explained_variance: Verified count differs, fully accounted for by recorded hand-ins.
criteria.unexplained_variance: Verified count differs and some gap remains with no record.

unexplained_gap.instructions: How large is the unexplained gap between account and verified count?
criteria: Nil: no unexplained gap between account and count
Minor: unexplained gap of one or two papers
Notable: unexplained gap of three to nine papers
Major: unexplained gap of ten or more papers

paperwork_shortfall.instructions: How many required closing items are missing or unsigned?
criteria: All required items present and signed
Exactly one required item missing or unsigned
Two required items missing or unsigned
Three or four required items missing or unsigned
Five or more required items missing or unsigned

factors.name: raw_variance
factors.description: Verified ballot count minus the account's expected papers in box; zero most often, small values common, occasional large values

factors.name: postal_handin_recorded
factors.description: Postal vote packs handed in at the station and placed in the box are recorded; when variance is positive the recorded number covers all or only part of it

factors.name: clerical_slip
factors.description: Account component lines do not sum to the declared total, or the reception transcription differs from the account, while papers physically reconcile

factors.name: missing_items
factors.description: Number of required closing items (seal record, spoilt envelope, unused papers packet, counterfoil packet, corresponding number list, declaration) absent or unsigned

factors.name: ballot_account_null
factors.description: The whole ballot paper account section arrives null; counts as one missing required item and forces reliance on counterfoil figures

factors.name: seal_mismatch
factors.description: Seal number recorded at close differs from the seal number found on arrival at the count centre

factors.name: seal_replacement_witnessed
factors.description: A replacement seal is logged before departure with a witness and a time; present with roughly half of seal mismatches, and sometimes with no mismatch as a decoy

factors.name: transit_gap_min
factors.description: Minutes between recorded close of poll and box receipt at the count centre

factors.name: remote_station
factors.description: Station is far from the count centre or reached by boat or single-track road, making a long transit gap plausible

factors.name: close_status
factors.description: How the poll closed: on time, legitimately extended for a queue at close, closed early with no flag, or close time not recorded

factors.name: agent_objection
factors.description: A candidate's agent present at sealing registered an objection flag, without resolving detail

factors.name: prior_queries
factors.description: Count of queries raised against this station at previous elections; a decoy that should not drive decisions alone

factors.name: po_first_time
factors.description: Presiding officer is serving for the first time; a decoy that raises suspicion without being evidence

sections.name: station
sections.description: Station code, ward, election date, distance and transport mode to count centre, presiding officer tenure, prior query count

sections.name: timeline
sections.description: ISO timestamps for scheduled close, actual close, queue flag and count, box departure and box receipt

sections.name: ballot_account
sections.description: Presiding officer's figures: papers received, issued, spoilt, tendered, unused, and declared expected papers in box; may be null

sections.name: seals_and_packets
sections.description: Seal number at close, replacement seal list, agent objection flag, postal hand-in count, required item list with present and signed flags

sections.name: verification
sections.description: Count centre figures: seal on arrival, ballots counted, counterfoils counted, reception transcription of account total

F311.rendering_notes: raw_variance appears only as the difference between verification.ballots_counted and ballot_account.expected_in_box (or, if the account is null, counterfoils_counted minus spoilt and tendered); never as a stored variance field. postal_handin_recorded shows as seals_and_packets.postal_handin_count (0 when absent); unexplained gap = |variance minus hand-ins|, so a partial hand-in count leaves a remaining gap. clerical_slip shows as ballot_account lines (issued, spoilt, unused, tendered) not summing to received, or verification.account_total_transcribed differing from ballot_account.expected_in_box while physical counts agree. missing_items shows in seals_and_packets.required_items, a list of objects {item, present, signed}; absent items have present false, unsigned have signed false; ballot_account_null renders the ballot_account section as null and the account item as present false. seal_mismatch shows as seals_and_packets.seal_at_close differing from verification.seal_on_arrival; seal_replacement_witnessed adds an entry to seals_and_packets.replacement_seals {seal_no, logged_at, witness_role} with logged_at before timeline.box_departed_at; when there is no mismatch a replacement entry may still appear as a decoy. transit_gap_min is derived from timeline.poll_closed_at and timeline.box_received_at; remote_station shows as station.distance_km above 25 and station.transport such as boat or single_track. Custody holds when seals match or a witnessed replacement seal matches the arrival seal, close time is recorded, and transit is at most 60 minutes, or at most 180 for remote stations. close_status: on_time gives poll_closed_at at scheduled close; queue_extension gives a later close with timeline.queue_at_close true and queue_count above 0 (legitimate); early_close gives a close before schedule with queue_at_close false; close_time_null sets poll_closed_at to null. agent_objection shows as seals_and_packets.agent_objection_at_sealing true with no detail. prior_queries and po_first_time are decoys in station.prior_query_count and station.po_tenure. Records never contain free text, status, risk, reconciled or custody fields; no field states a disposition, gap size or verdict.

F312.role: Grants monitoring officer at a community foundation reviewing interim progress reports before releasing the next payment tranche
F312.setting: A regional community foundation funds small neighbourhood projects (food clubs, youth sport, green spaces, digital inclusion) in tranches. Each grantee submits an interim progress report with spend by budget heading, receipts, and milestone status. The officer reviews one report at a time against the original award, approved variations and earlier reports, then decides whether the next tranche can be released.

unapproved_spend.instructions: Grant money was spent under a heading with no approval.

criteria.true: Spend on unlisted heading, no approved variation covers it
criteria.false: All spend sits within approved or variation-covered headings

tranche_decision.instructions: What should happen to this progress report and next tranche?

criteria.accept: Report reconciles; next tranche released with no follow-up needed.
criteria.accept_conditions: Tranche released; minor gaps must be fixed in next report.
criteria.hold: Tranche withheld until specific missing evidence or explanation arrives.
criteria.refer_panel: Escalated to grants panel over possible misuse or failed delivery.

variance_cause.instructions: What mainly explains the difference between profiled and reported spend?

criteria.no_variance: Reported spend within 10% of the profiled spend to date.
criteria.approved_change: Gap covered by an approved budget or timetable variation.
criteria.delivery_slip: No variation; gap matches late milestones deferring planned costs.
criteria.unexplained: Gap with no matching approved variation or milestone delay.

evidence_gap.instructions: How large is the gap between reported and receipted spend?
criteria: Gap is zero or under 1% of reported spend
Gap from 1% to under 5% of reported spend
Gap from 5% to 15% of reported spend
Gap above 15% of reported spend

milestone_delay.instructions: How overdue is the worst open milestone against its current due date?
criteria: On time: no open milestone past its current due date
Minor: worst open milestone 1 to 30 days overdue
Significant: worst open milestone 31 to 90 days overdue
Severe: an open milestone more than 90 days overdue

factors.name: receipt_gap_band
factors.description: Size of the difference between total_reported_gbp in the report and the sum of receipts in evidence, as a share of reported spend; boundary values sit exactly at 1%, 5% or 15%.

factors.name: gap_location
factors.description: Where the receipt gap arises: a receipt missing for one line, a receipt amount differing from its line, a duplicated receipt id, or spend_lines not summing to total_reported_gbp.

factors.name: offheading_spend
factors.description: A spend line or receipt uses a heading code absent from grant.approved_headings.

factors.name: heading_variation_on_file
factors.description: An approved budget variation in variations adds or reallocates to the off-heading code before the spend date; when off-heading spend is present this mitigates it.

factors.name: spend_profile_position
factors.description: Reported spend to date compared with the profile in grant.spend_profile for the report period end.

factors.name: budget_variation_covers_gap
factors.description: An approved variation re-profiles spend or extends timetable so the profile gap is accounted for; only meaningful when spend is outside 10% of profile.

factors.name: worst_overdue_days_original
factors.description: Days the worst open milestone is past its original_due at report.period_to; 0 means none overdue.

factors.name: revised_date_approved
factors.description: The worst overdue milestone has an approved timetable variation with a later revised_due, so lateness is measured against the revised date.

factors.name: partial_completion
factors.description: Open milestones show status in_progress with pct_complete between 30 and 90 rather than not_started.

factors.name: grant_ref_mismatch
factors.description: One receipt or the bank statement carries a grant_ref or payee account differing from grant.ref or grant.payee_account_last4.

factors.name: prior_issue_count
factors.description: Number of earlier reports in history with outcome held or accepted_conditions.

factors.name: outputs_shortfall_decoy
factors.description: Beneficiary counts in outputs fall below pro-rata target; half the time outputs.measurement_window_closed is false, making the shortfall uninformative.

factors.name: overdue_on_boundary
factors.description: The worst overdue figure measured against the current due date lands exactly on 30 or 31 or 90 or 91 days, or the variation approval date falls after period_to.

sections.name: grant
sections.description: Award details: ref, programme, award_gbp, period dates, approved_headings with budgets, spend_profile, tranches paid, payee account.

sections.name: report
sections.description: This report: report_id, period_to, submitted date, spend_lines by heading, total_reported_gbp, outputs counts.

sections.name: evidence
sections.description: Receipts list with id, heading, amount_gbp, date, grant_ref; bank_statement object or null.

sections.name: milestones
sections.description: List of milestones with original_due, revised_due, status, pct_complete, completed_on.

sections.name: variations
sections.description: List of variation requests: type, heading or milestone_id, new values, approved boolean, approved_on.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Prior reports with report_id, period_to, outcome and tranche released.

F312.rendering_notes: grant: ref, programme, award_gbp, period_start, period_end, approved_headings [{code, budget_gbp}], spend_profile [{to_date, cumulative_gbp}], tranches_paid_gbp, payee_account_last4. report: report_id, period_to, submitted, spend_lines [{heading, reported_gbp}], total_reported_gbp, outputs {participants, sessions, target_participants, measurement_window_closed}. evidence: receipts [{receipt_id, heading, amount_gbp, date, grant_ref}], bank_statement {account_last4, closing_balance_gbp} or null. milestones: [{milestone_id, original_due, revised_due (null unless a variation exists), status (complete/in_progress/not_started), pct_complete, completed_on}]. variations: [{var_id, type (budget/timetable), heading or milestone_id, new_budget_gbp or new_due, approved, approved_on}]; unapproved or pending variations are decoys and must not count. history: prior_reports [{report_id, period_to, outcome (accepted/accepted_conditions/held/referred), tranche_released_gbp}]. receipt_gap_band is realised by gap_location: a missing receipt for one line, a receipt amount differing from its spend line, a receipt_id listed twice, or spend_lines summing differently from total_reported_gbp; the reader must sum receipts and compare. offheading_spend appears as a heading code in spend_lines or receipts absent from approved_headings; heading_variation_on_file adds an approved budget variation for that code dated before the receipt date (sometimes a pending one as decoy). spend_profile_position compares total_reported_gbp with the spend_profile entry at period_to; budget_variation_covers_gap renders as an approved re-profile or timetable variation. milestone lateness is computed from report.period_to minus current due (revised_due if its variation is approved, else original_due); revised_date_approved controls this; partial_completion sets pct_complete. grant_ref_mismatch alters one receipt grant_ref or bank_statement.account_last4. Decoys: outputs shortfall while measurement_window_closed is false, completed milestones that were late (closed, so not counted), pending variations, small rounding pence differences. Answer logic: variance_cause is no_variance within 10% of profile, approved_change if an approved variation covers it, delivery_slip if no variation but open late milestones exist, else unexplained. tranche_decision: accept when gap under 1%, no uncovered off-heading spend, delay On time, no ref mismatch; accept_conditions for small gap or Minor delay or partial milestones; hold when one item (missing receipt, moderate gap, Significant delay) needs confirmation; refer_panel for large gap, uncovered off-heading spend with moderate or large gap, Severe delay without revision, or ref mismatch with prior_issue_count of 2 or more. No field may state a risk rating, a variance category, a gap percentage, an overdue day count or a recommended decision; all must be derived. No free-text notes or comments appear anywhere.

F313.role: Building control surveyor reviewing a single stage inspection record before deciding whether the builder may proceed to the next notifiable stage
F313.setting: A building control team inspects new-build and extension work at statutory stages (foundations, damp-proof course, drainage, frame, insulation, pre-plaster, completion). After each site visit an inspection record is compiled from the project file, the approved specification, the surveyor's site readings, the defect list, uploaded evidence and the builder's progress log. A reviewing surveyor reads one record at a time and decides whether the stage can be signed off, how serious any open defects are, and whether key claims about sequence and conformity are supported.

inspected_before_cover.instructions: The stage was inspected before follow-on work covered it.

criteria.true: Inspection date clearly precedes any logged covering work.
criteria.false: Covered first, same-day order unclear, or dates missing.

matches_spec.instructions: Measured as-built details match the approved specification for this stage.

next_step.instructions: What should happen next with this stage inspection?

criteria.sign_off: Stage compliant, fully evidenced; builder proceeds without any conditions.
criteria.conditional_pass: Only workmanship items open, evidence complete; check at next visit.
criteria.hold: No regulatory defect, but one certificate or confirmation awaited.
criteria.reinspect: Regulatory defect or early cover-up; revisit before work proceeds.

defect_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst defect still open at this stage?
criteria: None: no open defect recorded against this stage
Workmanship: open items all tagged workmanship, no regulation area
Regulatory: worst open item tagged energy, ventilation or drainage
Life_safety: any open item tagged structure or fire

pending_age.instructions: How long has this record been waiting without any decision?
criteria: Logged less than 24 hours ago
Waiting between one and seven days
Waiting between eight and thirty days
Waiting more than thirty days without decision

factors.name: stage_type
factors.description: Which notifiable stage the visit covered; changes which spec values, tests and covering events are relevant.

factors.name: cover_sequence
factors.description: Order of inspection versus the builder's logged covering event (concrete poured, trench backfilled, boards fixed, plaster started).

factors.name: spec_deviation
factors.description: How the surveyor's measured values differ from the approved specification for the stage.

factors.name: tolerance_boundary
factors.description: A measured value sits exactly on the stated tolerance limit, leaving conformity arguable.

factors.name: engineer_letter
factors.description: An engineer's or designer's letter accepting the as-built change is uploaded; mitigates structural or product deviations.

factors.name: variation_status
factors.description: Status of an amended-plan variation covering the deviation, if any.

factors.name: worst_open_defect
factors.description: Regulation area of the most serious defect genuinely still open at this stage.

factors.name: closed_status_conflict
factors.description: A defect marked closed in the list is described as still outstanding in a free-text note, or vice versa.

factors.name: evidence_gap
factors.description: What supporting evidence is missing for the stage.

factors.name: identifier_mismatch
factors.description: Plot or project reference on the inspection differs from the project section.

factors.name: prior_failed_visits
factors.description: Count of earlier failed or aborted visits for this same stage in the history list.

factors.name: note_hedging
factors.description: Surveyor note uses hedged wording about what could actually be seen, weakening any conformity claim.

sections.name: project
sections.description: Project ref, plot number, work type, plan approval status and any variation with its status.

sections.name: approved_spec
sections.description: Key approved values for the stage, e.g. depth_mm, insulation_mm, product, pipe_dia_mm, tolerance_mm.

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Visit date, stage, plot_ref, surveyor id, measured values with units, and free-text surveyor_note.

sections.name: defects
sections.description: List of items with id, reg_area tag, status open/closed, raised date and a one-line note.

sections.name: evidence
sections.description: Photo count and dates, test certificates with status, engineer letter, builder_message; may be null.

sections.name: site_progress
sections.description: Builder's logged covering events with dates and list of previous visits for this stage with results.

F313.rendering_notes: stage_type sets inspection.stage and decides which approved_spec fields and site_progress cover event appear (foundations: concrete_poured; drainage: backfilled plus air_test cert; insulation: boards_fixed; pre_plaster: plaster_started). cover_sequence appears only through comparing inspection.visit_date with site_progress.cover_events[].date: same_day_ambiguous gives equal dates with no times; cover_date_missing gives date null or the event absent. spec_deviation is shown by inspection.measured values against approved_spec: unit_only renders e.g. 0.15 m against 150 mm (conforming); within_tolerance stays inside approved_spec.tolerance_mm; material_shortfall falls below it; wrong_product names a different product string in measured.product. tolerance_boundary puts the reading exactly on the limit. engineer_letter appears as evidence.engineer_letter {date, scope} or null; variation_status as project.variation {ref, status} or null; a pending variation does not make a deviation conform. worst_open_defect is rendered through defects[] reg_area tags (workmanship, energy, ventilation, drainage, structure, fire) and status; closed_status_conflict marks an item closed while its note or the surveyor_note says it was not rectified, so the true open set must be inferred. evidence_gap: test_cert_pending gives a certificate with status awaiting; photos_absent gives photo_count 0; evidence_section_null makes the whole evidence section null. identifier_mismatch alters inspection.plot_ref against project.plot (typo: transposed digit). prior_failed_visits fills site_progress.previous_visits with result fail or aborted. note_hedging adds phrases like 'appeared to be' or 'partly obscured by spoil' to surveyor_note. Decoys: evidence.builder_message always sounds confident ('all done to drawings'), photo dates may precede the visit, defects of other stages may appear with status closed, and a high photo count never proves conformity. Records never contain an outcome, sign-off, severity, risk or compliance field; no field states whether work was covered early or matches spec.

F314.domain: gas safety certificates for rented homes
F314.role: Lettings compliance officer at a residential letting agency, checking each landlord's annual gas safety record before it is filed against a tenancy
F314.setting: The agency manages several thousand rented homes. For each property, the officer opens one structured gas safety record: the property's appliance inventory, the tenancy dates, the certificate as entered from the engineer's form, the per-appliance check results, the engineer's registration snapshot and the property's gas history. The officer must decide whether the certificate can be relied on, how urgently the next inspection is needed, how serious any open defect is, and what to do next. Records are assembled automatically from separate systems, so values often disagree between sections without any warning. No record contains free-text notes; every field is a code, number, date, boolean or null.

covers_all_appliances.instructions: Certificate covers every landlord gas appliance listed for the property.

engineer_valid.instructions: Engineer held valid registration for these appliance types on inspection date.

criteria.true: Registration active, identifiers match, categories cover every appliance checked.
criteria.false: Registration lapsed, identifiers differ, or a category is missing.

next_step.instructions: What should the compliance officer do with this certificate next?

criteria.accept: Everything reconciles and no defects are open; file as compliant.
criteria.accept_with_works: Certificate valid; only advisory items open, needing scheduled remedial works.
criteria.hold: Exactly one mismatch or missing detail needs landlord or engineer confirmation.
criteria.reinspect: Two or more gaps, expiry passed, or invalid engineer; reinspect fully.
criteria.emergency_isolation: Dangerous or at-risk appliance in service without isolation; disconnect immediately.

renewal_urgency.instructions: How soon must a fresh gas safety inspection be completed?
criteria: More than 60 days remain before true expiry
Between 29 and 60 days remain before expiry
Between 1 and 28 days remain before expiry
True expiry date reached or already passed

open_hazard.instructions: How serious is the worst defect still open on the certificate?
criteria: None: no open defects recorded on any appliance
Advisory: all open items classed not to current standard
Contained: worst open defect at risk, appliance isolated
Live risk: at-risk defect open, appliance still in service
Dangerous: immediately dangerous defect open on any appliance

factors.name: inventory_mismatch
factors.description: Disagreement between the property's appliance inventory and the appliances checked on the certificate: none, an inventory appliance absent from the certificate, an extra appliance on the certificate, the same appliance with a different location, or a serial or model mismatch suggesting a replaced unit

factors.name: tenant_owned_appliance
factors.description: Whether an inventory appliance missing from the certificate is flagged as tenant-owned, which takes it outside the landlord's duty and explains the gap benignly; drawn independently so the flag sometimes sits on an appliance that is on the certificate (decoy)

factors.name: date_misalignment
factors.description: Inconsistency among dates in different sections: none, certificate issue date earlier than the inspection date, printed expiry not equal to inspection date plus 12 months, or inspection dated after the tenancy start with no prior certificate in history

factors.name: days_to_true_expiry
factors.description: Days from the record's review date to the true expiry, computed as inspection date plus 12 months (not the printed expiry field); negative means expired

factors.name: renewal_booked
factors.description: Whether a renewal inspection appointment is already booked for a date before true expiry; lowers the action needed when expiry is close but does not change the urgency band

factors.name: engineer_status
factors.description: Registration state of the engineer on the inspection date: active with matching categories, lapsed before the inspection date, active but lacking a category for one appliance type checked, or licence number on the certificate differing from the registration snapshot

factors.name: worst_defect_class
factors.description: Highest defect classification recorded across appliance checks: none, not to current standard, at risk, or immediately dangerous

factors.name: defect_isolated
factors.description: Whether the appliance carrying the worst defect has a recorded isolation: supply turned off or capped, with a warning label code and responsible person acknowledgement; the alarming defect appears with and without this about equally

factors.name: remedial_completed
factors.description: Whether a remedial completion entry in history, dated after the inspection and signed by a registered engineer, closes the worst defect; sometimes the entry references a different appliance identifier and so does not close it

factors.name: combustion_reading
factors.description: Flue gas analyser reading on one appliance relative to the action threshold: normal, borderline near the threshold, high with a passing retest recorded, or high with no retest yet the appliance outcome marked pass

factors.name: prior_defect_count
factors.description: Number of earlier certificates in history that recorded a defect on the same boiler; alarming on its own but mitigated when the boiler install date postdates them

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether one deciding value is placed exactly on an anchor the scales leave open: true expiry exactly 28 or 60 days away, registration expiring on the inspection date itself, or a combustion reading equal to the threshold

sections.name: property
sections.description: Property reference, dwelling type, and appliance inventory list with ids, types, locations, serials, ownership and install dates

sections.name: tenancy
sections.description: Tenancy reference, start and end dates, occupancy status and review date of this record

sections.name: certificate
sections.description: Certificate number, inspection, issue and printed expiry dates, engineer licence number and overall outcome code

sections.name: appliance_checks
sections.description: Per-appliance results: appliance id, location, serial, flue type, analyser reading, threshold, retest, defect class, isolation status

sections.name: engineer
sections.description: Registration snapshot: licence number, business id, registration valid-from and valid-to dates, list of category codes

sections.name: history
sections.description: Prior certificates with dates and defect classes, remedial completion entries, and any booked renewal appointment

F314.rendering_notes: inventory_mismatch: compare property.inventory[] with appliance_checks[] by appliance_id, location and serial; missing_from_cert omits one inventory id from checks, extra_on_cert adds a check id not in inventory, location_mismatch keeps the id but changes location code (e.g. kitchen vs utility), serial_mismatch keeps id and location but alters serial and model, with no flag. tenant_owned_appliance: property.inventory[].owned_by = "tenant" on one appliance; when it is the missing one the gap is excused, otherwise it is a decoy. date_misalignment: certificate.inspection_date, certificate.issue_date, certificate.expiry_date, tenancy.start_date and history.prior_certificates[] dates; expiry_miscomputed prints an expiry a few days to several weeks off inspection plus 12 months. days_to_true_expiry: derived from certificate.inspection_date and tenancy.review_date only; never print a days-remaining field. renewal_booked: history.renewal_booking {date, status} or null. engineer_status: certificate.engineer_licence vs engineer.licence_no; engineer.valid_to vs inspection_date; engineer.categories[] vs appliance_checks[].appliance_type and flue_type. worst_defect_class: appliance_checks[].defect_class in {null, "NCS", "AR", "ID"}; defect_isolated: appliance_checks[].isolation {supply_off, capped, label_code, acknowledged_by_role}, partially filled in some records; remedial_completed: history.remedials[] {appliance_id, completed_on, engineer_licence}, which only closes a defect when appliance_id matches and completed_on is after inspection. combustion_reading: appliance_checks[].analyser {ratio, threshold, retest_ratio}; high_no_retest pairs a reading above threshold with outcome "pass". prior_defect_count: history.prior_certificates[].defects on the boiler id, with property.inventory[].install_date sometimes after them. boundary_case sets the relevant value exactly on 28 or 60 days, valid_to equal to inspection_date, or ratio equal to threshold. Decoys: certificate.overall_outcome (engineer's own pass/fail, can contradict appliance-level data), tenant ownership flags on certified appliances, old defects on replaced boilers, label codes without supply_off. The record never contains fields such as compliance_status, risk_level, urgency, recommended_action or hazard_rating, and no notes or free text of any kind.

F315.role: Street lighting fault controller in a local highway authority's lighting team, reviewing one fault report at a time to decide dispatch and closure
F315.setting: A council lighting contract receives fault reports on street lights from the public, police, night scouts and a central management system (CMS) that monitors individual lantern nodes. Each record pulls together the incoming report, the asset register entry, the latest CMS reading, the unit's job history, the current job card and any supply network information from the distribution network operator. The controller must judge whether the fault sits on the electricity supply or the unit, whether this is a repeat failure after a recent repair, what to do next, and how far the current job has progressed. Signals are spread across sections and must be cross-checked: dates against dates, CMS state against the report, neighbouring outages against the network log.

supply_side_fault.instructions: Evidence places the fault on the electricity supply, not the unit.

criteria.true: Network incident logged, or three or more adjacent units dark.
criteria.false: Single unit affected, or supply evidence missing or contradicted.

repeat_failure.instructions: This unit failed again within 84 days of a completed repair.

criteria.true: Completed repair dated within 84 days before this report.
criteria.false: No completed repair in window, or completion unconfirmed.

next_action.instructions: What should the controller do next with this fault report?

criteria.close_report: Unit confirmed burning, or an open job already covers it.
criteria.hold_verify: One confirmation, such as CMS reading or scout visit, needed first.
criteria.routine_repair: Confirmed fault, no live hazard; dispatch within standard window.
criteria.urgent_make_safe: Hazard not yet made safe, or critical site dark; attend within hours.

source_support.instructions: How many independent sources confirm the information in this record?
criteria: No independent source confirms the information
Exactly one independent source confirms it
Two or three independent sources confirm it
Four or more independent sources confirm it

repair_progress.instructions: How far has work progressed toward a verified repair of this fault?
criteria: No crew visit logged against this fault
Crew attended, fault still present or unresolved
Fix recorded on site, no CMS or scout confirmation
Fix recorded and confirmed by CMS or later scout

factors.name: dark_unit_count
factors.description: Number of units on the same feeder or street currently dark, shown via supply.feeder_units_dark and the length of report.units_reported; 2 is a deliberate boundary for the supply-side claim

factors.name: dno_incident_logged
factors.description: Whether the distribution network operator has an open incident reference for the area covering the unit

factors.name: cms_state
factors.description: Latest CMS reading for the unit's node, or the whole cms section null when the unit has no node fitted

factors.name: days_since_last_repair
factors.description: Days between the completion date of the most recent prior repair in history and report.received_at; values near 84 are common to create boundary cases

factors.name: last_repair_state
factors.description: State of the most recent prior job in history: fully completed, attended but never closed, or no prior job on record

factors.name: hazard_observed
factors.description: Physical hazard noted on the current job card or report fault code: none, column door missing, column knocked down or leaning, or cable exposed

factors.name: hazard_made_safe
factors.description: Mitigation: a crew, police or the network operator has already isolated supply or fitted a temporary cover, shown by job.made_safe and job.isolated_at

factors.name: site_category
factors.description: Location type recorded in the asset register; junctions, crossings and underpasses raise the importance of a dark unit, residential side roads lower it

factors.name: planned_works_active
factors.description: Mitigation: a scheduled lantern replacement or column test window covering the report date, which can explain a dark unit without a fault

factors.name: current_job_stage
factors.description: Progress of the current job: none raised or not attended, attended but unresolved, rectified with no confirmation, rectified and confirmed by later CMS burning or a scout pass

factors.name: dates_out_of_order
factors.description: Whether a job date is inconsistent, such as completed_at earlier than attended_at or attended_at earlier than report.received_at, undermining a claimed repair

factors.name: duplicate_of_open_job
factors.description: Whether job.linked_job_ref points to an already open job on the same unit raised before this report

factors.name: report_source
factors.description: Origin of the report; police and scout reports are trusted, public web reports sometimes give the wrong unit number

sections.name: report
sections.description: Incoming fault: ref, received_at, source, fault_code, units_reported list.

sections.name: asset
sections.description: Register entry: unit_id, column_type, lantern_type, site_category, install_year, planned_works.

sections.name: cms
sections.description: Latest node reading: node_id, status_code, last_comms_at, lamp_hours; null if no node.

sections.name: history
sections.description: List of prior jobs with job_ref, raised, attended, completed, outcome_code.

sections.name: job
sections.description: Current job card: job_ref, stage, attended_at, completed_at, hazard_code, made_safe, isolated_at, linked_job_ref.

sections.name: supply
sections.description: Network information: dno_incident_ref, dno_status, feeder_units_dark, feeder_id.

F315.rendering_notes: dark_unit_count appears as supply.feeder_units_dark (integer) and loosely as the number of ids in report.units_reported; public_web reports may list extra unit ids that cms shows burning (decoy). dno_incident_logged sets supply.dno_incident_ref to a reference string with dno_status 'open', otherwise null. cms_state maps to cms.status_code ('LF', 'OK', 'NC') with last_comms_at stale for no_comms; section_null makes the whole cms value null. days_since_last_repair and last_repair_state are rendered only as dates in history entries: completed jobs have a completed date, attended_not_completed has completed null, no_record gives an empty list; the controller must compute the gap to report.received_at. hazard_observed appears as job.hazard_code and/or report.fault_code ('DOOR', 'KNOCK', 'CABLE', or null); hazard_made_safe as job.made_safe boolean plus isolated_at timestamp, present with the same hazard about half the time. site_category is asset.site_category. planned_works_active fills asset.planned_works with window_start, window_end and work_type covering the report date, otherwise null. current_job_stage is shown through job.stage code ('RAISED', 'ATT', 'RECT') with attended_at/completed_at, and confirmation only via a cms OK reading after completed_at or a later scout entry in history; a RECT stage with cms null or NC is unconfirmed. dates_out_of_order inserts an impossible date sequence in job or the latest history entry. duplicate_of_open_job fills job.linked_job_ref with a ref matching an open history entry. report_source is report.source. Decoys: cms.lamp_hours high on healthy units, old install_year, alarming fault_code on reports where cms shows OK, feeder_units_dark of 2 without a network incident. No field may state a verdict: no 'supply_fault', 'repeat', 'priority', 'recommended_action' or 'progress' field; the answers must be inferred by comparing dates, codes and counts across sections. No free-text note fields.

F316.role: Winter service duty officer at a county highways depot, reviewing each completed gritting run log before sign-off
F316.setting: After every precautionary or reactive salting run, the vehicle's run log arrives at the duty desk. It combines the planned route, the latest road-surface forecast, telematics from the spreader, the salt loading and return figures, and short notes from the driver and depot. The duty officer checks one log at a time. They decide whether the log can be signed off, how much priority road was left deficient, how soon any gap will freeze, and what follow-up to order before conditions deteriorate.

treated_before_freeze.instructions: Every priority section was treated before its forecast freeze time.

criteria.true: All priority sections logged treated before freeze.
criteria.false: A priority section untreated, or treated after freeze.

salt_reconciles.instructions: Salt used matches approved spread rate across treated area, within 10%.

criteria.true: Net tonnage within 10% of expected usage.
criteria.false: Gap over 10%, or a tonnage figure unconfirmed.

follow_up.instructions: What follow-up should be ordered on this gritting run?

criteria.sign_off: Log accepted as complete; no further action required.
criteria.sign_off_noted: Accepted, with a minor discrepancy recorded for depot correction.
criteria.hold: Sign-off withheld until one missing confirmation is received.
criteria.partial_retreat: Named missed priority sections re-treated only; rest accepted.
criteria.full_rerun: Whole route re-treated because log cannot support coverage.

deficient_length.instructions: How much priority road was missed or treated below approved rate?
criteria: None: no priority road missed or undertreated
Minor: under 2 km of priority road affected
Moderate: 2 to 10 km of priority road affected
Major: over 10 km affected, or run abandoned

freeze_proximity.instructions: How soon will the earliest untreated priority road reach freezing?
criteria: No untreated priority road, or no freeze within 12 hours
Earliest untreated road freezes in 6 to 12 hours
Earliest untreated road freezes in 2 to 6 hours
Under 2 hours to freezing, or already frozen

factors.name: missed_extent
factors.description: Total length of priority road with no spreading recorded, or a logged rate below the approved rate, after closures and partner coverage are excluded

factors.name: missed_section_mitigated
factors.description: Whether an apparently untreated section is covered by a benign explanation: an approved road closure reference, or treatment logged by a second vehicle or a neighbouring authority under a mutual-aid agreement

factors.name: salt_gap
factors.description: Difference between net salt used (loaded minus returned) and the expected quantity (rate x treated length x width)

factors.name: rate_exception_approved
factors.description: Whether a reduced spread rate was authorised for this run, for example pre-wetted salt or residual salt from an earlier run. This changes the expected tonnage and can explain a low usage figure.

factors.name: finish_vs_freeze_min
factors.description: Minutes between the last priority section's treatment end time in telematics and that zone's forecast freeze time. Negative means treatment ended after the freeze time.

factors.name: hours_to_freeze_untreated
factors.description: Hours from log review time until the earliest untreated priority section's zone reaches 0°C under the latest forecast revision. Values cluster near the 2, 6 and 12 hour boundaries in some records.

factors.name: forecast_revised
factors.description: Whether a later forecast revision moved the freeze time. A warmer revision delays it and acts as mitigation; a colder revision brings it forward.

factors.name: crosscheck_mismatch
factors.description: Where a cross-section discrepancy sits, if anywhere. Some are trivial: registration spacing, or kg against tonnes with equal values. Others are material: a section code missing from telematics, or a log date differing from the telematics date.

factors.name: driver_note_type
factors.description: Content of the driver's free-text note

factors.name: follow_up_run_scheduled
factors.description: Whether a subsequent run covering the same route is already scheduled to finish before the forecast freeze time, which reduces the need for extra dispatch

factors.name: pending_confirmation
factors.description: Whether one key datum is awaiting confirmation, so that a single answer would settle the log. Examples: a weighbridge ticket number is null, or a partner authority's coverage is not yet confirmed.

factors.name: gps_dropouts
factors.description: Count of telematics signal dropouts during the run. Some overlap priority sections and leave coverage unproven; others fall on non-priority or transit stretches as decoys.

factors.name: nonpriority_untreated
factors.description: Whether some non-priority (secondary network) sections were left untreated. This is a decoy that does not count towards priority deficiency.

sections.name: run_header
sections.description: run_id, route_code, vehicle_reg, driver_id, run_date, decision_ref, run_type (precautionary/reactive), reviewed_at timestamp

sections.name: plan
sections.description: List of route sections: section_code, length_km, width_m, priority (P1/P2/secondary), planned_rate_gm2, forecast_zone

sections.name: forecast
sections.description: Per-zone rst_min_c and freeze_time, plus a revisions list with issued_at and the revised freeze_time per zone

sections.name: telematics
sections.description: List of treated segments (section_code, start, end, spread_on, logged_rate_gm2), a dropouts list with start, end and nearest_section, and the telematics vehicle_reg and date

sections.name: materials
sections.description: loaded_t, returned_t (null if unknown), weighbridge_ticket, rate_exception object (approved_by, reduced_rate_gm2, reason) or null

sections.name: notes
sections.description: driver_note and depot_note one-line free text, plus a closures list (section_code, closure_ref, authority) and partner_cover list

F316.rendering_notes: missed_extent appears only indirectly. Plan sections with priority P1/P2 either have no matching telematics segment, have spread_on false, or have logged_rate_gm2 below the planned rate (or below reduced_rate_gm2 where a rate_exception exists). The reader must sum the lengths. When missed_section_mitigated is true, the missing section appears in notes.closures with a closure_ref, or in partner_cover with a vehicle or authority and times. Such a section is not counted as missed. salt_gap is never stated: the reader computes expected tonnes as rate × length_km × 1000 × width_m / 1e6 over the treated sections, and compares it with loaded_t minus returned_t. figure_missing sets returned_t or weighbridge_ticket to null. rate_exception_approved fills materials.rate_exception; otherwise it is null. Where it exists, a low usage figure becomes consistent, and it changes which rate counts as undertreated. finish_vs_freeze_min arises from the last P1/P2 telematics end time against forecast.freeze_time for that section's zone, using the latest revision. hours_to_freeze_untreated is derived from run_header.reviewed_at and the revised freeze_time of the zone holding the earliest untreated priority section. forecast_revised adds an entry to forecast.revisions; the original freeze_time remains visible as a decoy. crosscheck_mismatch places the discrepancy between run_header and telematics (vehicle_reg, date), between plan and telematics (section_code such as A417-06 against A417-6, or a code absent altogether), or in materials units (loaded given in kg in the depot_note against tonnes in materials). reg_format and unit_kg_t with equal values are trivial; section_code and date_mismatch are material. driver_note_type gives one sentence. alarming_resolved reads like 'Spinner jammed near Holt Lane, cleared after ten minutes and section re-run', with a matching second telematics segment. alarming_unresolved reads like 'Chute blocked from the roundabout onwards, returned to depot' with no further segments. Routine and blank notes carry no signal. follow_up_run_scheduled appears in the depot_note, for example 'Run R2 booked out 03:30 on same route', with no explicit link to the gap. pending_confirmation appears as a null weighbridge_ticket, or a partner_cover entry with confirmed: false. gps_dropouts are listed with nearest_section; only dropouts on priority sections with no other segment evidence leave coverage unproven. Untreated nonpriority sections carry the 'secondary' priority and are decoys. No field may state completion status, deficiency, urgency, reconciliation result or recommended action. There are no fields like 'status: incomplete', 'missed_km' or 'priority: urgent'; every answer must be derived by comparing sections.

F317.role: Depot release examiner at a tram depot, who reviews one vehicle check record at a time before deciding whether a tram may leave for service.
F317.setting: A city tram depot where each tram gets a pre-service fitness check record. The record pulls together the vehicle's mileage, the current scheduled exam sign-offs, open and closed defects, repair work orders, engineering concessions and the planned duty. The examiner must reconcile these sections, notice missing or out-of-sequence steps and weigh mitigations such as valid concessions, recent brake tests or low-demand duties. Records contain no free text, only coded fields, identifiers, dates and numbers.

sc_defects_cleared.instructions: Every safety-critical defect on this tram is closed and properly retested.

release_decision.instructions: What release decision should the depot examiner make for this tram?

criteria.release: Fit for any planned duty with no restrictions applied
criteria.release_restricted: Runs only under a valid concession restriction or limited duty
criteria.hold: Kept in depot until one outstanding confirmation is recorded
criteria.withdraw: Taken out of service for repair before any running

worst_subsystem.instructions: Which subsystem holds the most severe unresolved defect on this tram?

criteria.none: No defect is open or awaiting retest on any subsystem
criteria.saloon_doors: Worst unresolved defect concerns passenger doors, interlocks or steps
criteria.pantograph: Worst unresolved defect concerns pantograph, collector head or roof gear
criteria.running_gear: Worst unresolved defect concerns wheels, bogies, suspension or couplers
criteria.brakes: Worst unresolved defect concerns service, emergency or track brakes

exam_completion.instructions: How much of the current scheduled exam is signed off?
criteria: Not started: no exam items signed off yet
Partial: fewer than half of exam items signed
Substantial: half or more signed, at least one outstanding
Complete: every exam item signed with a timestamp

exam_mileage.instructions: How close is the tram's odometer to its exam due mileage?
criteria: More than 500 km left before exam due
Between 0 and 500 km left before due
Past due mileage by 200 km or less
Past due mileage by more than 200 km

factors.name: km_to_exam_due
factors.description: Exam due mileage minus current odometer; negative means overrun. Values near 0, 500 and -200 sit on scale boundaries.

factors.name: odometer_disagreement
factors.description: Gap between vehicle odometer and the reading captured at release: none, trivial (under 20 km) or large (over 300 km), sometimes moving the record across a mileage threshold.

factors.name: exam_signed_fraction
factors.description: Share of current exam items that carry a signature and timestamp.

factors.name: exam_record_missing
factors.description: The exam section is null although an exam is due or open.

factors.name: worst_defect_subsystem
factors.description: Subsystem of the most severe unresolved defect, or none if all are cleared.

factors.name: worst_defect_state
factors.description: Lifecycle state of that defect: closed and retested, closed with no retest, open with work in progress, or open with no work order.

factors.name: worst_defect_safety_critical
factors.description: Whether the worst defect is flagged safety-critical rather than comfort or cosmetic.

factors.name: retest_out_of_order
factors.description: Retest timestamp precedes the work order completion time, so the retest cannot count.

factors.name: concession_present
factors.description: An engineering concession exists that covers the worst defect with a running restriction.

factors.name: concession_flaw
factors.description: When a concession is present, whether it is undermined: expired before departure, wrong fleet number, or wrong defect reference.

factors.name: wo_crossref_mismatch
factors.description: Work order linked to the defect disagrees with it: different subsystem code, or a defect reference not found in the defect list.

factors.name: planned_duty_type
factors.description: Duty the tram is booked for; shunt and spare duties are low-impact, peak diagrams high-impact.

factors.name: recent_brake_test_pass
factors.description: A passing brake test was logged within 24 hours before departure; mitigates brake concern but never closes a defect.

factors.name: balanced_signals
factors.description: Generator places mitigations and concerns in even balance, or a value exactly on a threshold, so judges may split.

sections.name: vehicle
sections.description: Fleet number, class, current odometer_km and last completed exam type and date.

sections.name: exam
sections.description: Current scheduled exam: exam_id, exam_type, due_at_km, opened_at and items list with item_code, result, signed_by, signed_at; may be null.

sections.name: defects
sections.description: List of defects with defect_id, fleet_no, subsystem, safety_critical, raised_at, status, closed_at, retest_at, retest_result.

sections.name: work_orders
sections.description: List of repair orders with wo_id, defect_ref, subsystem, opened_at, completed_at, status and parts list.

sections.name: concessions
sections.description: List of engineering concessions with conc_id, fleet_no, defect_ref, restriction_code, valid_from, valid_until; may be empty or null.

sections.name: release
sections.description: Planned duty: duty_id, duty_type, depart_at, odo_reading_km, brake_test_at, brake_test_result.

F317.rendering_notes: km_to_exam_due is never shown; it must be derived from exam.due_at_km minus vehicle.odometer_km. odometer_disagreement appears as release.odo_reading_km differing from vehicle.odometer_km; the later timestamped reading (release) is authoritative, so large gaps can shift the mileage band. exam_signed_fraction appears as the count of exam.items with non-null signed_by and signed_at against total items; some items carry a result but null signed_at as decoys. exam_record_missing renders exam as null while vehicle.last_exam_date is old. worst_defect_subsystem, worst_defect_state and worst_defect_safety_critical appear in one defects entry (status, closed_at, retest_at, retest_result, safety_critical) plus its linked work_orders entry; severity ranking for ties is safety_critical first, then earliest raised_at, and the generator avoids true ties. Closed cosmetic defects and closed-retested older defects act as decoys. retest_out_of_order shows defects.retest_at earlier than work_orders.completed_at. concession_present adds a concessions entry; concession_flaw shows as valid_until before release.depart_at, fleet_no differing from vehicle.fleet_no, or defect_ref not matching the defect. wo_crossref_mismatch shows work_orders.subsystem differing from defects.subsystem or defect_ref absent from defects. planned_duty_type appears as release.duty_type. recent_brake_test_pass appears as release.brake_test_result 'pass' with brake_test_at within 24 hours of depart_at; it appears with and without brake defects. No field states release status, fitness, overdue status, severity or completion percentage; there is no free text anywhere. Answers follow from reconciliation: a valid concession allows release_restricted but never makes the true/false claim true; one missing confirmation (closed without retest, small exam gap, trivial cross-reference error) points to hold; open safety-critical defects without valid concession, or overrun beyond 200 km, point to withdraw.

F318.role: Waterways asset inspector reviewing completed lock maintenance visit records before closure
F318.setting: An inland waterways operator sends crews to canal locks for inspections, planned repairs and reactive call-outs. Each visit produces a structured record covering the work order, the crew's visit log, materials issued and returned, post-work checks, and the lock's asset history. The inspector reviews one visit record at a time. They check that the sections agree with each other and decide whether the lock can return to navigation, what happens to the record, how soon a crew must return, and how many unexplained mismatches the record contains.

safe_to_reopen.instructions: The lock can safely return to unrestricted navigation now.

criteria.true: Defects cleared and post-work checks pass without contradictions.
criteria.false: Open defect, failed or missing check, or conflicting records.

record_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this visit record next?

criteria.close_visit: Records reconcile and ordered work complete; close as logged.
criteria.close_with_followup: Close visit but raise a separate minor follow-up job.
criteria.hold_query: Closure held until the crew confirms one specific point.
criteria.reopen_revisit: Visit not accepted; crew must return and redo work.

return_urgency.instructions: How soon must a crew next attend this lock?

criteria.next_scheduled: No extra attendance; the next planned inspection cycle suffices.
criteria.within_month: Extra attendance within 28 days for non-restricting outstanding work.
criteria.within_week: Return within 7 days; restriction or covered defect pending.
criteria.immediate: Crew needed within 24 hours; uncovered unsafe condition present.

affected_scope.instructions: How many people or units does this issue directly affect?
criteria: Affects one person or unit only
Affects two to five people or units
Affects six to twenty people or units
Affects more than twenty people or units

section_mismatches.instructions: How many unexplained mismatches exist between the record's sections?
criteria: No unexplained mismatches between any sections
Exactly one unexplained mismatch between sections
Exactly two unexplained mismatches between sections
Three or more unexplained mismatches between sections

factors.name: visit_type
factors.description: Kind of visit ordered. It shapes which tasks and checks are expected and how alarming an open defect is.

factors.name: tasks_ordered
factors.description: Number of tasks listed on the work order. These are reconciled against the task statuses in the visit log.

factors.name: completion_state
factors.description: True state of the ordered work: all done, some outstanding, a temporary fix only, or nothing done.

factors.name: parts_qty_mismatch
factors.description: Gap between parts recorded as fitted and parts issued minus returned. Ranges from none, to trivial pack rounding, to a moderate gap, to large missing items.

factors.name: hours_gap
factors.description: Difference in hours between the crew timesheet total and the arrival-to-departure span multiplied by crew size. Values under 0.5 are normal rounding.

factors.name: asset_ref_mismatch
factors.description: Whether the asset reference on a work-order task differs from the one on the matching post-check. An example is gate HG2 ordered but HG1 checked.

factors.name: post_check_result
factors.description: Outcome of the post-work functional check on the worked asset.

factors.name: leakage_ratio
factors.description: Measured gate leakage as a multiple of the lock's leakage limit. Values above 1.0 are the main alarming signal.

factors.name: leakage_mitigation
factors.description: Whether a benign explanation for the leakage reading is present. Examples are a reading taken while the river level was above the flood marker, or a gauge whose calibration expired before the reading and was re-read within limit.

factors.name: navigation_notice_in_force
factors.description: Whether a navigation closure or restriction notice is still in force and covers the outstanding work. If so, an open defect does not endanger boaters.

factors.name: deferral_approved
factors.description: Whether outstanding or temporary tasks carry a recorded supervisor approval reference and a deferral due date.

factors.name: prior_same_defect
factors.description: Number of visits in the past 12 months that logged the same defect code on the same asset.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether key values sit exactly on scale anchors. Examples are a leakage ratio of exactly 1.0, a deferral due date exactly 7 or 28 days out, or an hours gap of exactly 0.5.

sections.name: work_order
sections.description: Ordered visit: identifiers, visit type, task list with asset references and planned quantities, navigation notice.

sections.name: visit_log
sections.description: Crew attendance times, crew size, timesheet hours, and per-task status with deferral details.

sections.name: materials
sections.description: Parts issued from stores, returned to stores, and recorded as fitted per task.

sections.name: checks
sections.description: Post-work check results per asset, leakage reading and limit, river level, gauge calibration.

sections.name: asset_history
sections.description: Prior visits to this lock with defect codes, and the currently open defect list.

F318.rendering_notes:
Record layout by section:
- work_order: wo_id, lock_id, visit_type, raised (ISO date), tasks[{task_id, task_code, asset_ref, qty_planned}], nav_notice{in_force, from, to, scope_assets[]}.
- visit_log: arrived and departed (ISO datetimes), crew_size, timesheet_hours, task_status[{task_id, status: done|deferred|temp_fix|not_started, deferral_ref (string or null), deferral_due (date or null)}].
- materials: issued[{part_no, task_id, qty}], returned[{part_no, qty}], fitted[{part_no, task_id, qty}].
- checks: post_checks[{asset_ref, result: pass|pass_advisory|fail, checked_at}] (empty or missing entry when not_logged), leakage_ls, leakage_limit_ls, river_level_m, flood_marker_m, gauge_cal_due.
- asset_history: prior_visits[{date, asset_ref, defect_code}], open_defects[{defect_code, asset_ref, raised}].

How each factor appears:
- tasks_ordered is the length of work_order.tasks.
- completion_state appears only through task_status values.
- parts_qty_mismatch appears as fitted not equal to issued minus returned for a part number, or as a fitted part with no issue line.
- hours_gap appears as timesheet_hours against the visit span multiplied by crew_size.
- asset_ref_mismatch appears as a task asset_ref that differs from its post_check asset_ref.
- leakage_ratio appears as leakage_ls divided by leakage_limit_ls.
- leakage_mitigation appears as river_level_m above flood_marker_m, or as gauge_cal_due earlier than checked_at.
- navigation_notice_in_force appears as nav_notice.in_force with scope_assets covering the open asset and a to date after the visit.
- deferral_approved appears as a non-null deferral_ref and deferral_due.
- prior_same_defect is a count within prior_visits.
- boundary_case places values exactly on anchors.
- Mismatches that have a recorded explanation do not count as unexplained. Examples are a parts return dated after the visit, or a deferral with a ref.

Decoys: wo_id formats, lock flight number, crew_size changes with consistent hours, river_level_m when leakage is within limit, old closed defects in prior_visits, and trivial pack-rounding part quantities.

No field may state an answer. There must be no fields such as safe, urgency, mismatch_count, disposition, or overall status. No free-text notes appear anywhere.

F319.role: Blade integrity engineer reviewing individual rotor blade inspection reports
F319.setting: An onshore and offshore wind operator's blade engineering desk. Drone and rope-access crews inspect blades and submit one structured report per blade. The engineer reviews each report alone and decides on disposition, damage mechanism, worst defect depth and repair urgency. The engineer also judges whether damage has grown since the last inspection, using the asset record, the inspection details, the findings list, the inspection and repair history, and the maintenance and lightning-protection status.

damage_worsened.instructions: Damage on this blade has measurably worsened since the previous inspection.

disposition.instructions: What should happen to this blade following this inspection?

criteria.no_action: Findings within tolerance; normal inspection cycle continues unchanged.
criteria.monitor: Defect logged for targeted re-inspection; no repair yet warranted.
criteria.hold_confirm: One missing measurement, image zone or test needs confirming first.
criteria.planned_repair: Repair booked in next maintenance campaign; turbine keeps running.
criteria.stop_turbine: Structural threat present; turbine halted or curtailed until repaired.

damage_mechanism.instructions: Which damage mechanism best explains the most severe recorded finding?

criteria.coating_wear: Topcoat, filler or paint loss without erosion or impact pattern.
criteria.erosion: Rain or particle wear concentrated along the leading edge outboard.
criteria.lightning: Burn marks, receptor damage or exit holes from a strike.
criteria.structural: Cracks, delamination or bondline separation driven by fatigue loading.

defect_depth.instructions: How deep does the most severe recorded defect penetrate?
criteria: Surface: topcoat or filler only, laminate not exposed
Laminate: outer laminate exposed, no fibre breakage recorded
Fibre: fibre layers broken, core and spar cap intact
Core: damage reaches sandwich core or spar cap

repair_urgency.instructions: How soon must the worst finding be repaired or re-examined?
criteria: No action before next scheduled annual inspection
Action required within the next twelve months
Action required within the next three months
Action required within the next four weeks
Immediate action before the turbine runs again

factors.name: worst_depth
factors.description: True penetration of the most severe defect. Rendered only as measured depth_mm against laminate_thickness_mm, layers_affected and core_visible on the worst finding.

factors.name: mechanism
factors.description: Underlying cause of the worst finding. Inferred from zone, chord position, burn/soot flags, receptor status and crack orientation, never named directly.

factors.name: growth_state
factors.description: How the worst finding compares with the same zone and radius in the previous inspection. Covers no growth, growth under 10%, growth over 10%, or no comparable baseline.

factors.name: baseline_defect
factors.description: How a baseline can fail even when history exists. The previous record may cover a different zone, carry a date after the current inspection, or list a different blade serial.

factors.name: coverage_gap
factors.description: Some blade zones were not imaged or were imaged at unusable resolution. Shown as null image counts or a low quality score for one zone.

factors.name: mitigation_present
factors.description: A field that lowers concern about an alarming finding is present.

factors.name: mitigation_type
factors.description: Form the mitigation takes when present. Options are temporary leading-edge tape applied, turbine already curtailed, an approved OEM tolerance concession, or a passing ultrasonic check within 30 days.

factors.name: lps_result
factors.description: Lightning protection system continuity test outcome on this blade. A missing test matters when burn marks are present.

factors.name: repair_state
factors.description: Status of prior repair work on the worst finding: none started, partially completed, or completed but quality check not yet logged.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Puts the worst measurement within 5% of a depth or length threshold, or makes the inspector remark disagree with measured values. This leaves judges split.

factors.name: note_tone
factors.description: Tone of free-text inspector and work notes, independent of actual severity. Acts as a decoy.

factors.name: finding_count
factors.description: Number of findings listed on the blade. Mostly minor; a high count does not imply a deep worst defect.

factors.name: season_exposure
factors.description: Whether the site enters its high-wind or high-rain season within 60 days. Raises urgency for erosion and structural damage.

sections.name: asset
sections.description: Turbine and blade identity: site, turbine_id, blade_pos, blade_serial, blade_model, commissioned date.

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Current inspection: date, method, crew, zones list with image_count and quality_score, inspector_note free text.

sections.name: findings
sections.description: List of defects with zone, radius_m, chord_pos, length_mm, depth_mm, laminate_thickness_mm, layers_affected, flags, remark.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Previous inspection summary with date, blade_serial and matched findings, plus repair log entries.

sections.name: maintenance
sections.description: LPS test result, curtailment status, concessions, temporary measures, open work order and work_note free text.

F319.rendering_notes: worst_depth: the finding with the greatest depth_mm/laminate_thickness_mm carries the signal. Surface means depth_mm below 0.5 and layers_affected 0. Laminate means layers_affected 0 with laminate_exposed true. Fibre means layers_affected of 1 or more with core_visible false. Core means core_visible true or spar_cap_affected true. No category or grade field is ever shown. mechanism: erosion is shown as zone 'LE', radius_m in the outer third and chord_pos near 0. Lightning is shown as flags containing 'soot' or 'pinhole' near the tip receptor, with maintenance.lps.result possibly 'fail'. Structural is shown as flags 'crack' with orientation 'spanwise' or 'chordwise' at the trailing edge or bondline, or 'delam_tap'. Coating wear is shown as paint loss flags with no LE concentration. growth_state: history.previous.findings holds the same zone and radius_m with an older length_mm and depth_mm. Growth over 10% on either value marks worsening. no_baseline renders history.previous as null. baseline_defect: zone_mismatch means the previous inspection covered different zones only. date_out_of_order means history.previous.date is later than inspection.date. serial_mismatch means history.previous.blade_serial differs from asset.blade_serial. Any of these makes the worsening claim unsupported. coverage_gap: one entry in inspection.zones has image_count null or quality_score below 0.4. If that zone could hide the worst defect, hold_confirm is natural. mitigation: rendered in maintenance as temp_measures [{type:'le_tape', applied:date}], curtailment.active true with a reduced rpm_limit, concessions [{ref, max_length_mm}] where the finding is within the limit, or ndt_checks [{method:'UT', date, result:'pass'}] within 30 days. The same deep or long finding appears with and without mitigation at about equal rates. lps_result: shown as maintenance.lps.result pass, fail or null. Null is evidence of a missing step when soot flags exist. repair_state: history.repairs entries with status 'in_progress' and percent_complete give partial. A status of 'complete' with qc_signed null gives complete_unverified. boundary_case: the worst depth_mm sits within 5% of the laminate boundary, or a remark says 'cosmetic only' while layers_affected is 1. season_exposure: asset.site_season_start date within 60 days of inspection.date. Decoys: finding_count inflates with small paint chips. inspector_note and work_note follow note_tone, so alarmist wording may accompany surface damage and understated wording may accompany core damage. Image counts and drone model are irrelevant. No field ever states disposition, mechanism, depth category, urgency or a worsening verdict. Free-text fields are at most one or two sentences and describe observations, never conclusions about the five questions.

F320.role: Repair close-out reviewer in a water utility's distribution network team, checking each completed leak repair job record before it is signed off
F320.setting: A regional water utility logs every water main leak repair as a structured job record assembled from the field crew's handheld, the network control room's valve log, the laboratory sample system and the highways reinstatement tracker. Before a job can be closed, a reviewer must make five decisions about it. Is third-party damage supported? What close-out action is needed? What should the asset team do next for the main? How long was supply interrupted? How far has the site been reinstated? Records arrive one at a time. No section carries free-text notes, so every judgement rests on comparing coded fields, times, sizes, lists and flags across sections.

third_party_cause.instructions: The leak was caused by third-party damage to the main.

criteria.true: Strike marks or puncture, with works active before report.
criteria.false: No physical evidence, or works only after report.

closeout_action.instructions: What should happen to this repair job at close-out review?

criteria.close: Tests, samples and reinstatement all complete and mutually consistent.
criteria.close_with_actions: Safety checks confirmed; only reinstatement or record tidying outstanding.
criteria.hold: One test, sample or approval result still needs confirming.
criteria.reopen: Failed test, unapproved fitting or quality fault requires revisit.

asset_followup.instructions: What follow-up should the asset team plan for this main?

criteria.none: Isolated or external failure; no asset work beyond repair.
criteria.monitor: Deploy acoustic loggers and review the main after a quarter.
criteria.condition_survey: Commission an excavated condition survey of the affected section.
criteria.expedite_replacement: Bring the main's replacement forward in the capital programme.

interruption_duration.instructions: How long were customers without supply during the repair?
criteria: No properties lost supply at any point
Supply off for under 3 hours
Supply off for 3 to 12 hours
Supply off for more than 12 hours

reinstatement_stage.instructions: How far has the excavation site been reinstated?
criteria: Open: excavation still open or only fenced off
Temporary: backfilled with temporary surface, no permanent layer
Permanent: permanent surface laid, inspection not yet logged
Signed_off: permanent surface laid and inspection logged as passed

factors.name: fitting_size_mismatch
factors.description: Gap between the main's nominal diameter in the asset section and the size range of the repair fitting recorded in the repair section; trivial cases are unit rounding (inches vs mm) inside tolerance, major cases are a fitting range that excludes the main's outside diameter

factors.name: substitution_approved
factors.description: Whether an approved material or fitting substitution reference with an approver code exists for the repair, which legitimises a fitting or material that differs from the asset record

factors.name: pressure_test_outcome
factors.description: Sequence of post-repair pressure test results logged against the job

factors.name: water_quality_state
factors.description: Post-repair chlorine residual and bacteriological sample position: clear, low residual followed by flushing and a passing resample, low residual with no resample, or sample taken but result pending

factors.name: interruption_hours
factors.description: True supply interruption length from the first isolation valve shut to the last valve reopened affecting customers; zero when the repair was done under pressure or with full rezoning; values cluster near the 3 and 12 hour boundaries in a share of records

factors.name: estimate_drift
factors.description: How far the planned interruption estimate in the job section departs from the actual valve times; a decoy that is sometimes small and sometimes crosses a scale boundary

factors.name: reinstatement_state
factors.description: Actual reinstatement progress shown by the layer records and inspection list

factors.name: failure_cause
factors.description: True underlying cause of the leak, shown only through fracture type, strike marks, pipe wall condition and ground readings in the findings section

factors.name: third_party_permit_timing
factors.description: Whether street works permits within 50 m exist and whether their start date falls before or after the leak was first reported; post-report permits are decoys

factors.name: strike_marks_ambiguous
factors.description: Strike mark evidence is recorded as 'possible' rather than yes or no, or a puncture fracture sits on a heavily pitted pipe wall, leaving third-party cause contestable

factors.name: prior_bursts_5y
factors.description: Number of earlier bursts logged on the same main ID in the five years before this report

factors.name: replacement_scheduled
factors.description: Whether the main already sits in the capital replacement programme with a planned year, which lowers the need for new asset follow-up despite a poor burst history

factors.name: prior_external_share
factors.description: Proportion of prior bursts coded as third-party damage rather than structural failure; a high share mitigates an alarming burst count

factors.name: date_inconsistency
factors.description: Inconsistency between timestamps across sections: none, trivial (UTC vs local hour offset), or material (repair completed or surface laid before excavation opened, or inspection dated before surfacing)

sections.name: job
sections.description: Job reference, main ID, report and attendance timestamps, planned interruption estimate, nearby street works permits list

sections.name: asset
sections.description: Main material, nominal diameter, outside diameter in mm, install year, burst history list, replacement programme entry

sections.name: findings
sections.description: Excavation opened timestamp, depth, fracture type code, strike marks code, wall pitting grade, soil and ground movement readings

sections.name: repair
sections.description: Fitting type, fitting size range, fitting material, substitution reference, completion timestamp, pressure tests list

sections.name: network_ops
sections.description: Valve operations list with shut and open times, properties affected, rezoning flag, flushing log, water quality samples list

sections.name: reinstatement
sections.description: Surface layers list with type and laid date, highways inspection list with date and result

F320.rendering_notes: fitting_size_mismatch: asset.od_mm (number) versus repair.fitting_range_mm {min,max}; trivial_rounding shows the range given in inches in repair.fitting_range_in alongside a near-boundary mm value inside tolerance; major puts asset.od_mm outside the range. substitution_approved: repair.substitution_ref string plus approver_code when true, null when false; it appears with and without mismatches about equally. pressure_test_outcome: repair.pressure_tests list of {test_at, test_bar, held_mins, result}; not_logged is an empty list. water_quality_state: network_ops.samples list of {taken_at, cl_residual_mgl, bact_result} where bact_result is 'pass', 'fail' or null for pending; flushing appears as network_ops.flushing list of {start, end}; low residual is below 0.2 mg/l. interruption_hours: derived only from network_ops.valve_ops list of {valve_id, op:'shut'|'open', at, customer_side:boolean}; the reviewer must take the earliest customer-side shut and latest customer-side open; network_ops.rezoned true with no customer-side valves means zero interruption; network_ops.properties_affected is a count and never a duration. estimate_drift: job.planned_interruption_mins is a decoy that may sit on the other side of 3 h or 12 h from the real duration. reinstatement_state: reinstatement.layers list of {layer:'temp_bitmac'|'base'|'wearing_course', laid_on} and reinstatement.inspections list of {on, result}; open means an empty layers list with job.barriers_in_place true; there is no stage or status field. failure_cause and strike_marks_ambiguous: findings.fracture_type ('puncture','circumferential','longitudinal','joint_pullout','pitting_hole'), findings.strike_marks ('yes','no','possible'), findings.wall_pitting_grade 0-4, findings.ground_movement_mm; there is no cause field. third_party_permit_timing: job.nearby_permits list of {permit_ref, works_type, start_on, distance_m}, compared with job.reported_at; after_report permits are decoys. prior_bursts_5y and prior_external_share: asset.burst_history list of {on, cause_code}, including some entries older than five years as decoys. replacement_scheduled: asset.replacement_programme {scheme_ref, planned_year} or null. date_inconsistency: findings.excavated_at, repair.completed_at, reinstatement layer and inspection dates; trivial cases show a one-hour offset with a 'Z' suffix on one field only.
