criteria.fast_track: File complete, cover and weather confirmed, estimate within benchmark.
criteria.hold_for_info: Exactly one required document or confirmation is still outstanding.
criteria.field_inspection: File complete but damage extent or cost needs on-site assessment.
criteria.refer_investigation: Dates, statements or history conflict in ways suggesting misrepresentation.

source_support.instructions: How many independent sources confirm the information in this record?
criteria: No independent source confirms the information
Exactly one independent source confirms it
Two or three independent sources confirm it
Four or more independent sources confirm it

makesafe_urgency.instructions: How urgently does the property need emergency make-safe work?
criteria: No breach to roof, walls or windows recorded
Breach recorded, temporary repair already completed
Breach open, no temporary repair, home still habitable
Breach open and home recorded as unsafe to occupy

factors.name: weather_match
factors.description: How the automated weather lookup relates to the claimed loss date and location: qualifying gusts at a nearby station on the date, a qualifying event only at a distant station, no qualifying event, or a qualifying event one or more days away from the claimed date.

factors.name: report_lag_days
factors.description: Days between the claimed loss date and the date the claim was lodged; long lags are alarming but can be explained by the claimant being away.

factors.name: policy_status
factors.description: Policy state at the loss date: active with storm cover, within a lapse grace period, storm cover excluded by endorsement, or policy inception dated after the loss date (out-of-order dates).

factors.name: prior_condition_evidence
factors.description: What property history shows about the claimed damage area before the storm: nothing on file, a clean dated survey, a survey noting wear in the same area, or a previous claim on the same area that was never repaired.

factors.name: missing_item
factors.description: Which required intake item is absent: none, damage photos, contractor estimate (estimate section null), proof of ownership, or two items at once.

factors.name: estimate_ratio
factors.description: Contractor estimate total divided by the insurer's desk benchmark for the declared damage; high values are alarming.

factors.name: estimate_uplift_explained
factors.description: Whether the file carries a benign reason for a high estimate, such as listed-building materials, scaffold access or post-storm labour surcharge noted by the contractor and matched by a property flag.

factors.name: envelope_breach_state
factors.description: State of the building envelope after the storm: no breach, breach with temporary repair done, breach open but occupied, breach open and recorded unsafe.

factors.name: temp_repair_dated_before_loss
factors.description: Whether a temporary repair invoice is dated before the claimed loss date, an out-of-order sign that the damage predates the storm or the date is wrong.

factors.name: prior_claims_3y
factors.description: Number of storm or water claims on this property in the last three years.

factors.name: prior_claims_verified
factors.description: Whether earlier claims were each settled against a verified named storm, which lowers concern about repeat claiming.

factors.name: statement_consistency
factors.description: How the claimant's free-text statement fits the rest of the file: consistent, minor discrepancy (time of day, which room), or contradicting photos or weather timing.

factors.name: claimant_away_note
factors.description: Whether the statement explains a long reporting lag (holiday, hospital stay, second home), mitigating report_lag_days.

sections.name: policy
sections.description: Policy number, inception and renewal dates, status, storm cover flag, excess, endorsements.

sections.name: loss_report
sections.description: Loss date, lodged date, peril, damaged areas list, occupancy state, and the claimant's short free-text statement.

sections.name: weather_check
sections.description: Automated lookup: station id, distance_km, event_date, max_gust_mph, rain_mm, hail_flag, threshold_met.

sections.name: property_history
sections.description: Property flags, last survey date and short survey note, and a list of prior claims with dates, areas and settlement basis.

sections.name: estimate
sections.description: Contractor estimate total, desk benchmark, line items, temp repair entries with dates, short contractor note; null when not supplied.

sections.name: intake_docs
sections.description: Checklist of required documents with received booleans and received dates.

F331.rendering_notes: weather_match: weather_check.event_date and distance_km compared with loss_report.loss_date; confirmed_near = same date, distance_km under 10, threshold_met true; distant_station_only = threshold_met true but distance_km 25-60; date_offset = event_date 1-4 days from loss_date; no_event = threshold_met false with low max_gust_mph. Never write 'corroborated' anywhere. report_lag_days: shown only as loss_report.loss_date versus lodged_date. claimant_away_note appears as a sentence in loss_report.claimant_statement (e.g. 'We were abroad until the 14th and found the ceiling down on return'); absent otherwise. policy_status: policy.status plus policy.inception_date; incepted_after_loss shows an inception date later than loss_date with status 'active' (decoy: status looks fine); storm_excluded shows endorsements list containing 'END-STX storm exclusion' while storm_cover may be omitted. prior_condition_evidence: property_history.last_survey_date (before loss) and survey_note (e.g. 'rear slope tiles slipped, ridge mortar failing'); damaged areas in loss_report must be compared with note and prior_claims[].area; unrepaired_prior_claim shows a prior claim on the same area with settlement 'cash_settled' and no repair_completed date. missing_item: intake_docs entries with received false; contractor_estimate missing renders the estimate section as null; two_items marks two entries false. estimate_ratio: estimate.total versus estimate.desk_benchmark, never as a ratio field. estimate_uplift_explained: estimate.contractor_note mentions listed slate or scaffold access AND property_history.flags includes 'listed_building' or 'three_storey'; when false the note is generic or empty. envelope_breach_state: loss_report.occupancy ('occupied','occupied_partial','vacated_unsafe') plus damaged_areas items with breach booleans and estimate.temp_repairs entries; temp_repaired shows a dated tarpaulin or boarding line. temp_repair_dated_before_loss: a temp_repairs date earlier than loss_date. prior_claims_3y: length of property_history.prior_claims within three years; prior_claims_verified appears as each claim's settlement_basis 'named_storm_verified' versus 'claimant_account'. statement_consistency: the claimant_statement mentions a time, room or cause that matches or conflicts with damaged_areas, weather timing or photo captions in intake_docs. Decoys: vulnerable-occupant flag in loss_report, policy excess size, hail_flag when only wind damage is claimed, rain_mm alone, high prior_claims_3y when verified, long lag when explained. No field may state a route, urgency, fraud suspicion or pre-existence verdict; free text uses plain first-person or trade wording, at most one sentence each, three free-text fields maximum.

F332.role: Member loan underwriter at a community credit union, screening one personal loan application at a time before it reaches a lending decision
F332.setting: A regional credit union's lending desk receives personal loan applications for cars, home improvements and debt consolidation. Each application arrives as a structured file built from the application form, the member's account record, income verification documents, a credit bureau extract, the applicant's declared commitments and automated policy checks. Nothing on the file computes affordability or arrears for the underwriter. They must reconcile the sections themselves, weigh exceptions and arrangements that soften adverse signals, and decide the next step.

income_supported.instructions: Declared income is supported by current verified income within ten percent.

criteria.true: Current verified income within 10% of declared figure
criteria.false: Verification missing, stale, or more than 10% short

debts_disclosed.instructions: Every open bureau account appears among the applicant's declared commitments.

criteria.true: Each open bureau account matches a declared commitment
criteria.false: At least one open bureau account is undeclared

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this application next?

criteria.approve: File complete and consistent, all lending criteria met as requested
criteria.approve_conditions: File complete; approvable only with reduced amount or term
criteria.hold_docs: One missing or outdated document blocks a final decision
criteria.refer_committee: Complete file breaches a policy cap with no approved exception
criteria.decline: Affordability or credit history fails criteria even after restructuring

dti_level.instructions: How high is the post-loan debt-to-income ratio?
criteria: Low: monthly repayments under 25% of verified income
Moderate: repayments 25% to under 35% of verified income
High: repayments 35% to under 45% of verified income
Excessive: repayments 45% or more of verified income

arrears_depth.instructions: How deep was the worst countable arrears in 24 months?
criteria: No countable late payment in last 24 months
Worst countable late payment under 30 days
Worst countable late payment 30 to 89 days
Default recorded or 90 or more days late

factors.name: income_gap_pct
factors.description: Percentage by which verified gross monthly income falls short of declared income. Negative values mean verified income exceeds declared. Values near 10 sit on the question boundary.

factors.name: income_doc_state
factors.description: State of the primary income evidence: current (dated within 60 days of application), stale (older than 60 days) or missing entirely.

factors.name: second_income_verified
factors.description: Whether a second, separately verified income source exists, such as a pension or part-time role. It can close an apparent shortfall against declared income, which was entered as a combined figure.

factors.name: undeclared_account
factors.description: Whether the bureau shows an account missing from declared commitments, and its nature. Options are none, one closed or settled (does not breach), one small open account, or one large open account.

factors.name: post_loan_dti
factors.description: True post-loan ratio of total monthly repayments to verified monthly income. Repayments are counted after any consolidation payoffs. Values near 0.25, 0.35 and 0.45 make the scale contested.

factors.name: consolidation_payoff
factors.description: Whether the loan purpose is consolidation with named accounts to be paid off at drawdown. Those repayments leave the ratio, so a high-looking gross commitment total may be acceptable.

factors.name: worst_late_days
factors.description: Days past due of the worst late payment marker in the last 24 months, before any arrangement is taken into account.

factors.name: arrears_under_arrangement
factors.description: Whether the worst late marker falls inside a lender-agreed payment holiday or arrangement period. If so, it is not countable and the next-worst marker governs.

factors.name: policy_cap_breach
factors.description: Whether the requested amount or term exceeds the product cap. A breach can be on amount or on term; none means no breach.

factors.name: exception_approved
factors.description: Whether a logged, in-date exception approval covers the cap breach. It is present on about half of files with or without a breach, so it sometimes covers nothing.

factors.name: employer_name_variance
factors.description: How the employer name on the application compares with the payslip. It may match, differ trivially (abbreviation or suffix such as Ltd), or differ materially. A material difference makes the income evidence unusable until confirmed.

factors.name: member_tenure_months
factors.description: Months since the applicant joined the credit union. Shown prominently but does not change any answer; it acts as a reassuring or worrying decoy.

factors.name: share_balance
factors.description: Member's savings share balance in pounds. Large balances look reassuring but are not pledged and do not enter affordability, so this is a decoy.

sections.name: application
sections.description: Loan request: app_id, received date, product code, purpose, amount, term_months, monthly_instalment, payoff_accounts list, declared_gross_monthly, employer_declared.

sections.name: member
sections.description: Member record: member_no, joined date, share_balance, account_status, prior_loans list with outcome.

sections.name: income_verification
sections.description: List of verified income documents, each with type, source, employer_name, gross_monthly, doc_date and verified flag.

sections.name: credit_report
sections.description: Bureau extract: pulled date, accounts list (ref, lender, type, status open or closed, balance, monthly_payment, late_markers with month, days_past_due and arrangement_flag), defaults list.

sections.name: declared_commitments
sections.description: Applicant's own list of existing debts: lender, type, balance, monthly_payment, plus housing_cost.

sections.name: policy_checks
sections.description: Product caps (max_amount, max_term_months), cap_check results, and exceptions list with exception_id, covers, approved_by role, expiry date.

F332.rendering_notes:
Income: declared_gross_monthly sits in application. Verified figures sit in income_verification documents; derive the gap from income_gap_pct. When second_income_verified is true, add a second verified document whose sum with the first closes part or all of the apparent gap; never print a total. For income_doc_state stale, set doc_date more than 60 days before application.received. For missing, omit the primary payslip, leaving only a bank statement with verified false, or an empty list. employer_name_variance shows as employer_declared versus the payslip employer_name: identical, an abbreviation or suffix change, or a different company.

Debts: undeclared_account adds a bureau account whose lender and balance have no counterpart in declared_commitments. closed_settled shows status closed with balance 0. open_small and open_large show status open with a balance and monthly_payment. Declared and bureau entries for the same debt may differ slightly in balance (bureau date lag); that is decoy noise, not non-disclosure. Lender names may be abbreviated differently across sections.

Affordability: post_loan_dti is rendered only through monthly_payment values (bureau open accounts plus any undeclared ones), housing_cost, monthly_instalment and verified income. The reviewer must compute it; no ratio field exists. When consolidation_payoff is true, purpose is consolidation and payoff_accounts lists bureau refs, which must be excluded. Sometimes one listed ref does not match any bureau account and cannot be excluded.

Arrears: worst_late_days appears as a late marker in credit_report accounts. When arrears_under_arrangement is true, that marker carries arrangement_flag true and its month falls inside the agreed period; the next-worst marker is unflagged and governs the arrears level. Defaults appear in the defaults list with date.

Policy: policy_cap_breach shows as amount or term_months exceeding policy_checks caps. cap_check lists only check names with values compared, never pass or fail verdicts. exception_approved adds an exceptions entry, which may cover the wrong item (term when amount is breached) or have expired; only an in-date entry covering the actual breach counts.

Decoys: member_tenure_months (joined date), share_balance, prior_loans outcomes and bureau balance lag do not change answers.

The record must never contain fields stating income adequacy, a debt-to-income ratio, an arrears grade, a disclosure verdict, a risk rating or a recommended decision. All answers must be derived by reconciling sections.

F333.role: Residential deposit and condition reviewer for a university-linked student accommodation provider. Reviews each completed room inspection record before deposit deductions are released and works orders are confirmed.
F333.setting: Each record covers one study bedroom or studio at one inspection point, usually checkout and sometimes mid-term or pre-arrival. It brings together the room details, tenancy dates, the signed check-in inventory, the inspector's checkout grading with photo references, the draft deposit charge lines and the estate works-order log for that room. The reviewer compares these sections to decide whether charges stand, what caused the condition found, how serious the worst defect is and how far the draft charges depart from what the evidence supports. Nothing in the record states a conclusion. Every judgement rests on cross-checking grades, dates, amounts and works orders.

checkin_clean.instructions: Every charged item was graded undamaged in the check-in inventory.

disposition.instructions: What should happen to this inspection report and its charges?

criteria.approve_as_drafted: Findings and charge lines match evidence; release without any change.
criteria.adjust_and_approve: Some lines wrong but correctable using figures already in record.
criteria.hold_for_evidence: Exactly one missing photo, signature or grade must be obtained.
criteria.order_reinspection: Checkout inspection missing, misdated or multiply incomplete; room needs revisiting.

main_cause.instructions: What is the main cause of the room's recorded condition findings?

criteria.no_defect: Checkout grade equals check-in grade for every listed item.
criteria.fair_wear: Grade drops by one step, consistent with tenancy length.
criteria.resident_damage: Newly damaged at checkout with no related prior works order.
criteria.building_fault: Defect matches a works order for fabric or building services.
criteria.prior_occupant: Defect already graded damaged in this tenancy's check-in inventory.

defect_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst defect recorded at this inspection?
criteria: Cosmetic: no defect, or marks and scuffs only
Functional: an item needs repair, room still usable
Habitability: fixture failure stops normal use of room
Safety: smoke detector, electrics or fire door failed

charge_gap.instructions: How large is the gap between proposed and evidenced charges?
criteria: Proposed total equals evidenced line totals exactly
Difference from £0.01 up to £25.00
Difference above £25.00 up to £100.00
Difference above £100.00

factors.name: inspection_type
factors.description: Which inspection point the record represents. Checkout carries charges. Mid-term and pre-arrival mostly carry works orders and zero or small charges.

factors.name: checkin_inventory_state
factors.description: Completeness of the check-in inventory: complete and signed on arrival, partial (some items ungraded), missing (section null), or signed more than 7 days after tenancy start.

factors.name: prior_damage_on_charged_item
factors.description: Number of charged items that were already graded damaged or fair at check-in, contradicting a charge for new damage.

factors.name: charge_discrepancy
factors.description: Size of the mismatch between the summary total and the evidenced line totals. Sources vary: wrong qty, unit rate differing from the rate card, a line total arithmetic error, or a line for an item absent from the checkout grades.

factors.name: worst_defect_tier
factors.description: Tier of the worst defect at checkout grading.

factors.name: true_cause
factors.description: Underlying cause of the main finding, expressed only through grade changes, tenancy length and works-order links.

factors.name: predating_works_order
factors.description: A works order for the same location and category was raised before tenancy start. This mitigates a resident-damage reading of an alarming defect.

factors.name: safety_fault_remedied
factors.description: For safety or habitability defects, a works order shows the fault completed the same day with a passed retest. This lowers urgency but not tier.

factors.name: photo_coverage
factors.description: Share of charged lines that carry at least one photo reference in the checkout inspection.

factors.name: tenancy_months
factors.description: Length of occupancy in months, which shifts one-step grade drops between fair wear and resident damage.

factors.name: date_out_of_order
factors.description: Checkout inspection dated before key return, or check-in inventory dated after the first works order raised by the resident.

factors.name: deposit_dispute_lodged
factors.description: Resident has lodged a deposit dispute. The flag alone decides nothing but raises the cost of approving weak charges.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Places a value on a scale edge: gap exactly £25.00 or £100.00, one-step grade drop at 6 months, or a works order location naming an adjacent room. Judges may split.

sections.name: room
sections.description: room_id, block, room_type, floor, next_occupancy_date, rate_card_ref.

sections.name: tenancy
sections.description: resident_ref, start_date, end_date, key_return_date, deposit_held, deposit_dispute_lodged.

sections.name: checkin_inventory
sections.description: signed_date, signed_by_resident, items list of item_code, location, grade (good/fair/damaged/null); may be null.

sections.name: checkout_inspection
sections.description: inspection_type, inspection_date, inspector_id, items list of item_code, location, grade, defect_category, photo_refs.

sections.name: proposed_charges
sections.description: lines of item_code, reason_code, qty, unit_rate, line_total; summary_total; rate_card_ref.

sections.name: works_orders
sections.description: list of wo_id, raised_date, location, category, priority_code, status, completed_date, retest_passed.

F333.rendering_notes: inspection_type sits in checkout_inspection.inspection_type. checkin_inventory_state shows as a complete item list with signed_date at or before tenancy.start_date. A partial state has null grades on some items, missing makes checkin_inventory null, and signed_late puts signed_date more than 7 days after start_date. prior_damage_on_charged_item appears only by matching item_code between proposed_charges.lines and checkin_inventory.items, where grade is fair or damaged; it is never flagged. charge_discrepancy is placed in varying spots: qty in a line differing from the count in checkout items, unit_rate differing from the rate card (shown via a line with a mismatched rate_card_ref), line_total not equal to qty times unit_rate, summary_total not equal to the sum of lines, or a line for an item graded good at checkout. Evidenced charges are lines whose item is graded worse at checkout than check-in and carry a photo_ref. worst_defect_tier is conveyed through defect_category values (scuff, stain, broken_fitting, no_hot_water, heater_fail, smoke_detector_fail, socket_scorched, fire_door_closer) and never through a severity field. true_cause emerges from grade pairs, tenancy_months (start to end dates) and works-order links by location and category. predating_works_order is a works order with raised_date before start_date at the same location. safety_fault_remedied is status completed, with completed_date equal to inspection_date and retest_passed true. photo_coverage shows as empty photo_refs lists. date_out_of_order shows only as raw dates. Decoys: priority_code on unrelated works orders, next_occupancy_date pressure, deposit_dispute_lodged, high deposit_held, and works orders for other locations in the room. No field states disposition, cause, severity rank, evidenced total or gap, and no free-text notes appear anywhere.

F334.role: League discipline desk officer reviewing referees' post-match misconduct reports before sanctions are issued
F334.setting: A regional amateur football league runs a discipline desk. After each fixture where a referee shows a caution or a dismissal, the referee files a misconduct report. The report holds fixture details, both team sheets, an incident list with free-text referee notes, any written observations from assistant referees or the fourth official, submission metadata and the season history of the sanctioned players. One desk officer reviews each report alone. The officer must decide four things: whether every sanctioned player is reliably identified, what to do with the report next, which category the most serious incident belongs to, and how many unexplained inconsistencies the report contains. Reports are never pre-labelled. The officer has to cross-check the sections against each other, weigh explanations such as logged substitutions or approved filing extensions, and recognise when a single query to the referee is enough or when a hearing is needed.

identity_confirmed.instructions: Every sanctioned player is identified consistently across all report sections.

criteria.true: Shirt, name and registration agree, or a log explains it.
criteria.false: At least one sanctioned identity unresolved or only possibly correct.

next_step.instructions: What should the discipline desk do with this report next?

criteria.process_as_filed: Accept the report unchanged and issue standard sanctions now.
criteria.correct_and_process: Fix a clerical error resolvable from other sections, then issue.
criteria.hold_clarification: Pause until the referee answers one specific written query.
criteria.refer_to_panel: Send to a hearing; facts or tariff exceed desk powers.

incident_category.instructions: Which category does the report's most serious incident fall into?

criteria.caution_only: No dismissals; every sanction recorded is a caution.
criteria.second_caution: Dismissal arising solely from two cautions in one match.
criteria.direct_dismissal: Straight dismissal for conduct towards players, not match officials.
criteria.official_targeted: Dismissal for conduct directed at a referee or assistant.

affected_scope.instructions: How many people or units does this issue directly affect?
criteria: Affects one person or unit only
Affects two to five people or units
Affects six to twenty people or units
Affects more than twenty people or units

mismatch_count.instructions: How many unexplained cross-section mismatches does the report contain?
criteria: No unexplained mismatches between any sections
Exactly one unexplained mismatch between sections
Two or three unexplained mismatches between sections
Four or more unexplained mismatches between sections

factors.name: identity_mismatch
factors.description: Kind of disagreement between a sanctioned player's incident entry and the team sheet: none, shirt number differs, name spelling differs, registration id differs, or player absent from sheet

factors.name: identity_explained
factors.description: Whether another section benignly explains the identity mismatch, such as a substitution log showing a shirt swap, a kit-change note, or an alias recorded on registration

factors.name: most_serious_offence
factors.description: True category of the gravest incident in the report

factors.name: code_text_conflict
factors.description: Whether the referee's free-text note describes conduct different from the offence code entered, e.g. code shows dissent but note describes pushing an assistant

factors.name: minute_conflict
factors.description: Disagreement between incident minute and substitution log or official notes: none, small gap of 1 to 3 minutes, or impossible timing such as player already substituted off

factors.name: official_accounts
factors.description: How assistant or fourth official observations relate to the referee's account of the gravest incident

factors.name: submission_delay_hours
factors.description: Hours between final whistle and report submission; the league deadline is 48 hours

factors.name: extension_approved
factors.description: Whether a filing extension was approved for this fixture, making a late submission benign

factors.name: amendment_count
factors.description: Number of times the referee amended the report after first submission; each amendment has a short reason

factors.name: clarification_state
factors.description: Status of any query already raised to the referee: none raised, raised and awaiting reply, or reply logged

factors.name: note_specificity
factors.description: Quality of the referee's free-text note on the gravest incident: specific with conduct and target, vague, or blank

factors.name: prior_cautions
factors.description: Season caution count of the gravest-incident player before this match; five triggers an accumulation ban, otherwise a decoy

factors.name: sanctioned_count
factors.description: Number of distinct players sanctioned in the report

sections.name: match
sections.description: Fixture id, competition, ISO date, kick-off time, venue, referee id and assistant ids.

sections.name: team_sheets
sections.description: Home and away lists of players with shirt number, name, registration id, starter flag, plus substitution log entries.

sections.name: incidents
sections.description: List of sanctions with minute, team, shirt, player name, registration id, offence_code, target and a short ref_note.

sections.name: officials_notes
sections.description: List of observations from assistants or fourth official, each with author role, minute and one-sentence text.

sections.name: submission
sections.description: Submitted_at timestamp, deadline_at, extension_ref (null if none), amendments list with reason, and query status.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Per sanctioned player: season cautions, prior dismissals, current suspension flag; referee's season report correction count.

F334.rendering_notes: identity_mismatch appears only by comparing incidents[].shirt/player_name/reg_id with team_sheets entries; when identity_explained is true a substitution log entry, a kit-change line in officials_notes or an alias on the sheet resolves it, otherwise nothing does. most_serious_offence is never stated as a category: it shows through offence_code (invented codes such as CAU-UB, CAU-DIS, DIS-2C, DIS-SFP, DIS-VC, DIS-OFA), the target field (player, spectator, referee, assistant, null) and ref_note wording. When code_text_conflict is true the ref_note describes conduct inconsistent with the code (e.g. DIS-VC with target player but note mentions shoving the assistant), so the true category must be read from the text. minute_conflict shows as incident minute versus team_sheets substitution minutes or officials_notes minutes. official_accounts is rendered as officials_notes text that echoes, omits or disputes the referee's version. submission_delay_hours is implied by submitted_at versus match date and kick-off plus deadline_at; extension_approved fills extension_ref with an id, else null. amendment_count is the length of submission.amendments, each with a one-line reason, some benign (typo in venue) and some substantive (changed offence code). clarification_state appears as submission.query_status (none, sent, answered) with the answer text if answered. note_specificity governs ref_note length and detail; blank is an empty string. prior_cautions sits in history and is a decoy unless reaching 5. Decoys: referee correction count, venue name variations, kick-off time format, prior dismissals of unsanctioned players, benign amendments. Explained mismatches do not count toward mismatch_count. No record contains fields such as identity_status, recommended_action, category, severity or discrepancy_count; answers must be derived by cross-checking.

F335.role: Continuity scheduler reviewing one booked segment in a station's playout log before lock
F335.setting: A regional commercial radio group builds hourly playout logs days in advance. Each booked segment (commercial, sponsored feature, pre-recorded show, news package or promo trailer) arrives as a structured record from the traffic system. Before the log locks for automated playout, the continuity scheduler checks the segment on its own. The checks cover asset readiness, length against the booked slot, music rights, sponsor and regulated-copy approval, and content rules for the daypart. The scheduler then decides what happens to the segment.

asset_fits.instructions: The segment's asset is verified and fits its booked slot length.

disposition.instructions: What should the scheduler do with this booked segment?

criteria.approve: No unresolved checks; air exactly as booked without changes.
criteria.approve_adjusted: Air after applying logged trim point or adjacent filler absorption.
criteria.hold: Exactly one confirmation outstanding and playout lock still ahead.
criteria.reschedule: Content valid elsewhere; move to compliant or later slot.
criteria.pull: Remove from log; asset or clearance unusable in any slot.

main_blocker.instructions: Which single issue most blocks the segment from airing as booked?

criteria.no_blocker: Every check resolved; segment ready and cleared as booked.
criteria.asset_timing: Asset readiness or length is the only unresolved blocker.
criteria.rights_clearance: Rights or approval gap blocks airing; no content breach.
criteria.content_compliance: Content conflicts with slot rules and has no approved exception.

lock_urgency.instructions: How close is this segment to its playout lock deadline?
criteria: Routine: playout lock more than 72 hours away
Soon: playout lock between 24 and 72 hours away
Pressing: playout lock between 2 and 24 hours away
Critical: lock under 2 hours away or already passed

open_checks.instructions: How many prerequisite checks remain unresolved for this segment?
criteria: No prerequisite checks remain unresolved
Exactly one prerequisite check remains unresolved
Exactly two prerequisite checks remain unresolved
Exactly three prerequisite checks remain unresolved
Four or more prerequisite checks remain unresolved

factors.name: item_type
factors.description: Kind of booked segment. Sets which clearances apply: commercials and sponsored features need copy or sponsor approval, while shows and trailers carry music rights.

factors.name: hours_to_lock
factors.description: Hours between review.reviewed_at and the lock time. Lock time is slot.slot_start minus slot.lock_lead_h. Values cluster near 2, 24 and 72 so that some records fall on a boundary.

factors.name: asset_status
factors.description: State of the audio asset. A missing asset appears as item.asset as null. An uploaded but unchecked asset has qc_passed false and no qc_at.

factors.name: duration_delta_s
factors.description: Asset duration minus booked slot length, in seconds. Tolerance is plus or minus 2 seconds, so values of 2 to 4 sit on the boundary.

factors.name: trim_point_logged
factors.description: Asset has a logged edit point that brings it within tolerance. Mitigates an overrun.

factors.name: flex_filler_adjacent
factors.description: The next item is a flexible sweeper or bed that can absorb or pad the difference. Mitigates a length mismatch of up to 15 seconds.

factors.name: rights_state
factors.description: Music rights status for tracks within the asset.

factors.name: copy_approval_state
factors.description: Sponsor or regulated-copy approval, for commercial and sponsored items. In the approved_after_slot case the approval is dated after slot_start, which is out of order and therefore unresolved.

factors.name: content_flag
factors.description: Content attribute that may conflict with the slot's daypart rules. Examples are explicit lyrics before the watershed, an alcohol product in a children's daypart, and political material during an election restriction.

factors.name: compliance_exception_approved
factors.description: An approved exception covering the content flag for this slot, such as an edited radio version on file or compliance sign-off. Mitigates the content conflict.

factors.name: asset_replaced_after_approval
factors.description: Change log shows the asset version was replaced after clearance or approval was granted, so that approval no longer covers what will air.

factors.name: clearances_missing
factors.description: The whole clearances section is null. Rights and copy approval are then unresolved wherever they apply.

factors.name: prior_clean_airings
factors.description: Count of earlier airings of the same asset without incident. This is a decoy: it reassures but resolves no current check.

sections.name: slot
sections.description: Booked position: station_id, slot_start, slot_length_s, daypart, watershed_active, election_restriction, lock_lead_h.

sections.name: item
sections.description: Segment details: item_type, booking_ref, asset object (asset_id, version, duration_s, qc_passed, qc_at, edit_points list) and content_tags list.

sections.name: clearances
sections.description: Approvals: music_rights object, copy_approval object, exceptions list with scope and approved_at; may be null.

sections.name: schedule_context
sections.description: Neighbouring items: prev_item and next_item with type, flex flag and min/max duration.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Asset airing count, last_aired, and change_log list of timestamped version or approval events.

sections.name: review
sections.description: Review metadata: reviewed_at, reviewer_desk, log_version.

F335.rendering_notes:
hours_to_lock is never stated. The reader must compute it as slot.slot_start minus slot.lock_lead_h, compared with review.reviewed_at.

Asset and length:
- asset_status shows up as item.asset being null (missing), or as qc_passed false with qc_at null (unchecked).
- duration_delta_s shows only as item.asset.duration_s against slot.slot_length_s.
- trim_point_logged appears as an entry in item.asset.edit_points with an out_s value that brings duration within 2 seconds; otherwise edit_points is empty or holds unusable cue points (decoy).
- flex_filler_adjacent appears as schedule_context.next_item.flex true, with min/max duration bounds that cover the gap.

Clearances:
- rights_state appears in clearances.music_rights.status, with request_logged_at for pending and valid_until earlier than slot_start for expired.
- copy_approval_state appears in clearances.copy_approval.status and approved_at. For approved_after_slot the status reads approved, but approved_at is later than slot.slot_start.
- content_flag appears as a tag in item.content_tags, to be read against slot.daypart, watershed_active or election_restriction. A tag with no matching restriction is a decoy.
- compliance_exception_approved appears as an entry in clearances.exceptions whose scope matches the tag and slot.
- asset_replaced_after_approval appears in history.change_log as a version_replaced event timestamped after the approval event. Its item.asset.version differs from the version named in the approval.
- clearances_missing makes clearances null.

Decoys: prior_clean_airings appears in history.airing_count and last_aired, and is a decoy. prev_item details, log_version and reviewer_desk are also decoys.

Counting open_checks: there are five prerequisite checks: asset verified, length fit, music rights, copy approval and content compliance.
- not_required and not_applicable count as resolved.
- An approved exception resolves the content check.
- A trim point, or a covering filler, resolves the length check.
- Pending, expired, awaiting, rejected, approved_after_slot, stale approval or a null section counts as unresolved.
- A missing asset leaves both the asset and the length checks unresolved.

main_blocker precedence: content_compliance over rights_clearance over asset_timing.

No record may contain a status, risk, urgency, disposition or 'ready' field that states an answer. Every judgement must come from comparing fields across sections.

F336.role: Restoration quality-control technician at a film preservation archive, checking one completed or in-progress restoration job record before the digital master is released and the original element is returned to storage
F336.setting: Each record is a restoration job for one catalogued film element (one title, one or more reels). The technician reconciles the catalogue entry against the inbound condition survey, the work log, the delivered scan files and the storage history, then decides whether the master can be released, what happens to the original element, how much work remains and how far the element's acetate decay has really progressed.

master_complete.instructions: Delivered master accounts for every catalogued frame and is checksum-verified.

criteria.true: Frames reconcile or gap covered; checksums verified.
criteria.false: Unexplained frame or reel gap, or checksum unverified.

job_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this restoration job next?

criteria.release_master: Everything reconciles and signed off; release master to access copies.
criteria.hold_confirm: Only one confirmation, retest or sign-off stands between job and release.
criteria.partial_rework: Redo specific failed or missing steps; accepted reels and work stand.
criteria.full_rework: Delivered output unusable as a whole; restart from a fresh scan.

element_handling.instructions: Where should the original element go after this check?

criteria.return_vault: Back to standard cold store on the normal re-inspection cycle.
criteria.shorter_cycle: Back to cold store with re-inspection due within twelve months.
criteria.isolate: Separate ventilated store, kept away from other acetate reels.
criteria.urgent_duplicate: Copy to new stock before any further storage or handling.

steps_outstanding.instructions: How many planned restoration steps remain unfinished on this job?
criteria: No planned steps left unfinished
Exactly one planned step unfinished
Two or three planned steps unfinished
Four or more planned steps unfinished

decay_stage.instructions: How advanced is the original element's confirmed acetate decay?
criteria: None: latest valid AD strip reading is 0
Early: latest valid AD strip reading is 1
Active: latest valid AD strip reading is 1.5
Severe: latest valid AD strip reading 2 or higher

factors.name: frame_gap
factors.description: Difference between catalogued frame count (length_ft x 16 for 35mm, x 40 for 16mm) and the sum of delivered frames: none, trivial leader-only gap up to 24 frames, moderate gap of 25 to 480 frames, or large gap of over 480 frames

factors.name: reel_count_mismatch
factors.description: Catalogue lists more reels than appear in the delivered file list, with no reel-level entry explaining the shortfall

factors.name: gap_exception_approved
factors.description: An approved exception documents known lost footage whose frame range matches the observed gap; present about half the time a gap exists, sometimes with a range that only partly covers the gap

factors.name: checksum_status
factors.description: State of fixity verification across delivered files: all verified, at least one mismatch, or verification not yet run on one or more files

factors.name: steps_unfinished
factors.description: Number of planned work-log steps whose status is not done (queued, in_progress or failed)

factors.name: ad_strip_raw
factors.description: Highest acid-detection strip reading recorded for the element across survey and storage history

factors.name: reading_in_excursion
factors.description: The highest strip reading was taken during a logged vault temperature or humidity excursion or maintenance window, which makes it suspect

factors.name: retest_logged
factors.description: A later strip retest under normal vault conditions is recorded, usually one step lower than the suspect reading; absent retest after an excursion leaves the reading needing confirmation

factors.name: shrinkage_pct
factors.description: Base shrinkage percentage measured at inbound survey; values near 1.0 and 1.5 sit on handling boundaries

factors.name: shrinkage_remeasure_drift
factors.description: Difference between survey shrinkage and the remeasurement logged at the scan step: none, small (under 0.2 points) or large (0.5 points or more)

factors.name: preservation_duplicate_exists
factors.description: A preservation duplicate on new stock is already held for this element, which lowers the need for urgent duplication

factors.name: curator_signoff_pending
factors.description: Curatorial sign-off on the restoration is not yet recorded even though technical work may be finished

factors.name: base_type
factors.description: Film base of the element; polyester elements carry an AD reading of 0 and test_required false, acting as a decoy against shrinkage values

sections.name: catalogue
sections.description: Accession entry: acc_id, title_ref, gauge, base, reels, length_ft, fps_nominal, element_type.

sections.name: inbound_survey
sections.description: Condition survey at intake: survey_date, shrinkage_pct, ad_strip, splices, perf_damage_ft, odour_logged, test_required.

sections.name: work_log
sections.description: List of planned steps with step, reel_no, status, started, finished, operator_id, remeasured_shrinkage_pct.

sections.name: delivery
sections.description: Delivered scan files: list of reel_no, frames, resolution, fps, duration_s, checksum_ok; plus delivered_on.

sections.name: storage
sections.description: Vault history: vault_id, ad_readings list (date, value), excursions list (start, end, type), duplicate_held.

sections.name: approvals
sections.description: Exceptions list (exc_id, type, reel_no, frame_from, frame_to, approved_on) and curator_signoff date or null.

F336.rendering_notes: frame_gap is never stated: the reader must compute catalogue.length_ft x frames-per-foot (16 for 35mm, 40 for 16mm) and compare with the sum of delivery[].frames; trivial gaps sit at reel heads. reel_count_mismatch shows as catalogue.reels greater than the number of distinct delivery reel_no values. gap_exception_approved appears as an approvals.exceptions entry of type lost_footage whose frame_from/frame_to range matches, partly matches or does not exist for the gap. checksum_status shows per file as checksum_ok true, false or null. steps_unfinished is the count of work_log entries with status other than done; finished dates may be null. ad_strip_raw appears as the highest value in storage.ad_readings or inbound_survey.ad_strip; reading_in_excursion means its date falls inside a storage.excursions window; retest_logged adds a later lower reading outside any excursion. shrinkage_pct is inbound_survey.shrinkage_pct and shrinkage_remeasure_drift shows in work_log[].remeasured_shrinkage_pct on the scan step. preservation_duplicate_exists is storage.duplicate_held; curator_signoff_pending is approvals.curator_signoff null. Decoys: delivery fps and duration_s may differ (24 vs 25 fps) while frames still match; resolution varies freely; splice counts, perf_damage_ft and odour_logged vary without deciding the questions on their own; excursions sometimes exist on dates with no readings; polyester elements show shrinkage but AD 0. No field may state completeness, disposition, handling destination, decay stage or a count of unfinished steps; no free-text notes are included.

F337.role: Seismic network data quality analyst reviewing one station-day quality-control packet at a time before archive release
F337.setting: A regional seismograph network collects continuous waveform data from broadband and strong-motion stations. Each day an automated QC pass assembles a packet per station covering metadata, acquisition statistics, waveform metrics, the field maintenance log and short operator notes. The analyst checks that the sections agree, decides whether the day's data can be released to the public archive, and judges how much of the data is actually usable. Summary fields are produced by different subsystems and are not always in step with each other or with the field log.

response_valid.instructions: Instrument response metadata matches the sensor currently installed at the site.

criteria.true: Serial, gain and epoch agree with latest install.
criteria.false: Metadata conflicts with, predates or lacks logged install.

gaps_explained.instructions: Every data gap overlaps a logged outage, visit or telemetry fault.

disposition.instructions: What should happen to this station-day's waveform data in the archive?

criteria.release: No unresolved issues; data fit for unrestricted archive use.
criteria.release_flagged: Problems confined to identified segments; flag those, publish the rest.
criteria.hold: Usability depends on one pending confirmation or metadata correction.
criteria.quarantine: Data untrustworthy throughout; withhold entirely and request field repair.

usable_fraction.instructions: What share of expected channel-hours is usable after removing gaps and faults?
criteria: Minimal: under 50% of expected channel-hours usable
Low: 50% to under 90% usable
High: 90% to under 99% usable
Complete: 99% or more channel-hours usable

pending_age.instructions: How long has this record been waiting without any decision?
criteria: Logged less than 24 hours ago
Waiting between one and seven days
Waiting between eight and thirty days
Waiting more than thirty days without decision

factors.name: sensor_metadata_state
factors.description: Whether the response metadata reflects the sensor actually installed: no swap, swap with metadata updated, swap with stale metadata still pointing at the old serial, or a mistyped serial differing by one character from the log.

factors.name: maintenance_log_present
factors.description: Whether the maintenance_log section is populated; when false it is null, so swaps or outages cannot be verified and absence counts against explanatory claims.

factors.name: gap_coverage
factors.description: How the gaps in the acquisition list relate to logged outages: no gaps, all gaps inside logged outages, at least one gap with no matching log entry, or a gap that overruns its logged outage by a few minutes.

factors.name: true_usable_fraction
factors.description: Actual fraction of expected channel-hours free of gaps, dead channels and clipping, derivable only by combining the gap list with per-channel QC flags.

factors.name: completeness_summary_drift
factors.description: Percentage points by which the acquisition completeness_pct summary overstates the completeness implied by the gap list; zero in many records, a decoy when non-zero.

factors.name: timing_quality
factors.description: GPS timing state over the day: locked throughout, intermittent lock with short drift, or lock lost for hours making timestamps doubtful.

factors.name: calibration_status
factors.description: State of the daily or post-visit calibration pulse: passed, not yet run, failed, or dated before the logged sensor swap so it tests the old sensor.

factors.name: noise_excess_db
factors.description: How far the channel noise PSD sits above the station baseline in dB; high values look alarming whether or not a benign cause is documented.

factors.name: benign_noise_cause_logged
factors.description: Mitigation: whether an operator note or log entry documents a known temporary noise source (roadworks, storm, nearby generator) covering the noisy period.

factors.name: operator_note_consistency
factors.description: Whether operator notes are absent, agree with the structured data, or assert something the data contradicts (e.g. 'sensor swapped Tuesday' when the log dates it Thursday).

factors.name: dead_channels
factors.description: Number of components flagged dead or flatlined in qc_metrics for most of the day.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: When true, the generator places the usable fraction within half a point of a level threshold or a gap edge within two minutes of its outage edge, leaving judges split.

sections.name: station
sections.description: Network and station codes, digitiser, and per-channel sensor serial, gain, azimuth and response epoch start.

sections.name: acquisition
sections.description: Station-day date, expected channel-hours, completeness_pct summary, gap list per channel, GPS lock percentage.

sections.name: qc_metrics
sections.description: Per-channel noise PSD deviation, spike count, dead flag, clipped minutes, and calibration pulse date and result.

sections.name: maintenance_log
sections.description: Field visit and outage entries with dates, actions, installed serial and outage windows; null when unavailable.

sections.name: operator_notes
sections.description: One to three one-sentence free-text remarks from station operators or field technicians.

F337.rendering_notes: station.channels[] lists cha, sensor_serial, gain_counts_per_ms, azimuth_deg, response_epoch_start (ISO). sensor_metadata_state shows only by comparing station.channels[].sensor_serial and response_epoch_start with the latest maintenance_log entry where action='sensor_swap' (sensor_serial_installed, date): swap_stale keeps the old serial and an epoch before the swap date; serial_typo differs by one character; never add a 'metadata_ok' field. acquisition has day, channel_hours_expected, completeness_pct, gaps[{cha,start,end}], gps_lock_pct; gap_coverage is visible only by matching gaps against maintenance_log outage_start/outage_end (minor_overrun: gap ends 3-15 minutes after the logged window, under 2 minutes when boundary_case). completeness_summary_drift inflates completeness_pct above what the gap list implies, so completeness_pct is a decoy and the gap list plus qc flags govern usable_fraction. true_usable_fraction is never printed; it is implied by gap durations, qc_metrics[].dead=true channels (dead_channels) and clipped_minutes. timing_quality appears as gps_lock_pct and timing_quality_mean (lost_hours under 80% lock). calibration_status appears in qc_metrics.cal_pulse {date, result}: not_run gives date null and result null; predates_swap gives a date earlier than the swap log date with result 'pass', a decoy. noise_excess_db shows as qc_metrics[].psd_dev_db; benign_noise_cause_logged appears only as an operator note or log note naming the source and time window, present in about half of noisy records. operator_note_consistency: contradicts_data notes state a date, serial or outage that disagrees with the log. When maintenance_log_present is false the section is null and swaps or outages cannot be confirmed, so gaps_explained is false whenever gaps exist. Expected answers: disposition release only with no unresolved conflict; release_flagged when faults are confined to listed segments or channels; hold when exactly one item (stale metadata, missing cal pulse, unlogged gap) needs confirmation; quarantine when timing lost for hours, all channels dead or calibration failed. Records never contain fields like 'quality', 'risk', 'disposition', 'usable_pct' or 'explained'; dates are ISO, unknowns null, numbers numeric.

F338.role: Network quality assurance officer reviewing field calibration visit records for ambient gas analysers
F338.setting: A regional ambient air monitoring network runs gas analysers for NO2, O3, SO2 and CO at roadside, urban background and industrial sites. Field technicians visit each site to run as-found checks, adjust the analyser, then run as-left checks against a certified reference standard. The visit record is uploaded to the network's data management system. The QA officer reviews each record one at a time. They decide whether data collected since the previous visit can stand, whether the reference standard was valid, what happens to the record next, how much prior data must be flagged, and how quickly a technician must return.

data_accepted.instructions: Data since the previous visit can be accepted without correction or flagging.

reference_valid.instructions: The reference standard used was certified, in date and correctly identified.

criteria.true: Identifier, units and expiry agree with the certificate record.
criteria.false: Identifier, units or expiry disagree, or certificate details absent.

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this calibration visit record next?

criteria.close_visit: Results acceptable and no prior data needs flagging.
criteria.close_flagged: Results acceptable after adjustment, but some prior data needs flagging.
criteria.hold: Keep open; exactly one confirmation or document still outstanding.
criteria.recalibrate: Calibration incomplete or as-left failed; repeat on site.
criteria.withdraw: Analyser faulty beyond site adjustment; remove for workshop repair.

flag_extent.instructions: How many days of prior data require flagging or correction?
criteria: No days of prior data require flagging
One to seven days require flagging
Eight to thirty days require flagging
More than thirty days require flagging

return_urgency.instructions: How soon must a technician return to this site?
criteria: Routine: next scheduled visit, no additional attendance needed
Planned: extra visit needed in eight to thirty days
Prompt: return needed in three to seven days
Urgent: return needed within one to two days
Immediate: return needed on the same day

factors.name: pollutant
factors.description: Gas measured by the analyser; sets typical span concentration, units and tolerance conventions.

factors.name: as_found_ratio
factors.description: Worst as-found deviation from reference expressed as a multiple of the point tolerance; below 1 is within tolerance.

factors.name: as_left_status
factors.description: Outcome of as-left checks after adjustment: all within tolerance, marginal (within 10% of the limit), one point outside, or not recorded.

factors.name: cylinder_id_mismatch
factors.description: Agreement between the reference identifier logged in the checks and the one in the reference section: identical, transposed digit, or a different standard entirely.

factors.name: cert_expiry_offset_days
factors.description: Certificate expiry date minus visit date; negative means the standard had expired, values near zero sit on the boundary.

factors.name: unit_mismatch
factors.description: Reference concentration logged in the checks in different units from the certificate (ppb against ppm, or ppm against mg/m3) without conversion.

factors.name: interim_autocheck_pass
factors.description: Whether nightly automatic span checks between visits passed until shortly before the visit, limiting the window over which drift could have affected data.

factors.name: drift_explanation
factors.description: Benign context for an out-of-tolerance as-found result: none, a logged maintenance window, a recorded enclosure temperature excursion, or an approved extended service interval.

factors.name: days_since_last_visit
factors.description: Interval between the previous valid calibration and this visit, which bounds how much data may need flagging.

factors.name: visit_completeness
factors.description: How much of the planned check sequence was carried out: full sequence, zero only, multipoint missing, or aborted by power loss.

factors.name: prior_fail_count
factors.description: Number of failed as-found or as-left results for this analyser in the past twelve months of history.

factors.name: timestamp_mismatch
factors.description: Agreement between the visit date and times and the timestamps on individual check points: consistent, minutes outside the visit window, or a different calendar day.

factors.name: site_priority
factors.description: Regulatory tier of the site; higher tiers raise the cost of lost data and the urgency of return visits.

sections.name: site
sections.description: Site identifier, pollutant, site tier, scheduled service interval and any approved interval extension.

sections.name: visit
sections.description: Visit identifier, date, start and end times, technician code, sequence status and maintenance window flag.

sections.name: reference
sections.description: Reference standard identifier, certified concentration, unit, certificate number and expiry date.

sections.name: checks
sections.description: List of as-found and as-left points with type, reference concentration, unit, reading, tolerance and timestamp.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Previous visit date and outcome, twelve-month result list and nightly autocheck log entries.

sections.name: instrument
sections.description: Analyser serial, model, firmware, last service date and enclosure temperature minimum and maximum.

F338.rendering_notes: pollutant appears as site.pollutant and drives typical span values in checks. as_found_ratio is never stated: render as_found points in checks with ref_conc, reading and tolerance (absolute, in the point's unit), so the reader must compute deviation; spread the worst point across zero, span or precision types. as_left_status is rendered through the as_left points in the same way; not_recorded means the as_left list is empty or the points have null readings. cylinder_id_mismatch shows as checks[].ref_id differing from reference.standard_id (one transposed digit, or a wholly different identifier); in most records they match exactly. cert_expiry_offset_days is rendered only through reference.cert_expiry against visit.date. unit_mismatch shows as checks[].unit differing from reference.unit while ref_conc carries the unconverted figure. interim_autocheck_pass appears as history.autochecks, a list of dated entries with result pass or fail; when true, passes run until a few days before the visit; when false, the list has early failures or a gap. drift_explanation appears as visit.maintenance_window true, instrument.enclosure_temp_max above 30 or min below 10, or site.approved_interval_days greater than site.service_interval_days; when none, these fields sit at ordinary values. days_since_last_visit is visit.date minus history.last_visit_date. visit_completeness appears as visit.sequence_status (complete, partial, aborted) together with which check types are present in checks; a partial label alone does not say which points are missing. prior_fail_count is the count of fail entries in history.results. timestamp_mismatch appears as checks[].ts outside visit.start to visit.end, or on a different date. site_priority is site.tier. Decoys: instrument.firmware recently changed, technician code, certificate number format, instrument.last_service_date, pass entries far back in history, and small rounding differences under 1% between reading and ref_conc that do not matter. Never include fields that state an answer, such as overall_result, data_valid, flag_days, revisit_due or reference_ok. Deviation percentages and expiry status are never precomputed. No free-text fields: all content is identifiers, numbers, dates, enums and booleans, with null for unknown values.

F339.role: Adoption counsellor at a rehoming centre, reviewing one submitted adoption application at a time against the requested animal's placement profile before a match is confirmed
F339.setting: A mid-sized animal rehoming centre takes adoption applications through its case system. Each application links one household to one animal. The counsellor compares the household's details with the animal's placement requirements and checks the status of the home visit, landlord consent, references and prior adoption history. They also check any behaviour-team overrides, then decide what happens next. Records are structured only, with no free-text notes.

home_visit_valid.instructions: A current home visit confirms the stated household details.

criteria.true: Visit completed within 180 days, after submission, details matching.
criteria.false: Visit missing, pending, stale, misdated, or details differ.

species_consent.instructions: Documented permission exists to keep this species at the address.

criteria.true: Owner occupier, or landlord consent naming this species.
criteria.false: Consent absent, pending, or covering another species only.

disposition.instructions: What should happen with this application at this stage?

criteria.decline: A disqualifying finding stands with no recorded override or mitigation.
criteria.hold_pending: At least one required check or document remains outstanding.
criteria.approve_conditional: All checks complete; a waived or minor mismatch needs agreed conditions.
criteria.approve: All checks complete and no unresolved mismatch remains.

source_support.instructions: How many independent sources confirm the information in this record?
criteria: No independent source confirms the information
Exactly one independent source confirms it
Two or three independent sources confirm it
Four or more independent sources confirm it

requirement_conflicts.instructions: How many placement requirements do the household details contradict?
criteria: No placement requirement contradicted by household details
Exactly one placement requirement contradicted by household details
Exactly two placement requirements contradicted by household details
Three or more placement requirements contradicted by household details

factors.name: home_visit_state
factors.description: State of the home visit: done within 180 days, done but older than 180 days, booked but not done, not started, or the visit object null

factors.name: visit_date_out_of_order
factors.description: The home visit is dated before the application submission date, so it cannot have assessed this application

factors.name: visit_detail_mismatch
factors.description: The household details recorded by the visit differ from those the applicant declared, such as a different adult count or garden status

factors.name: tenure_consent
factors.description: Housing tenure and landlord consent status for keeping the animal

factors.name: tenancy_pet_clause
factors.description: The tenancy record carries a general pets-permitted flag that names no species, a partial mitigation when no consent record exists

factors.name: contradicted_requirements
factors.description: Number of the animal's placement requirements that the household data contradicts, e.g. a child under the minimum age, a cat present, hours alone over the maximum, or no garden

factors.name: behaviour_override
factors.description: A behaviour-team override is recorded for one contradicted requirement, approving the placement despite it

factors.name: threshold_boundary
factors.description: A household value sits exactly on a requirement limit, such as the youngest child's age equalling the minimum or hours alone equalling the maximum

factors.name: reference_status
factors.description: Completion of personal references and the vet reference

factors.name: prior_returns
factors.description: The applicant's history of returning previously adopted animals and the coded reason

factors.name: trusted_repeat_adopter
factors.description: The applicant has an earlier completed adoption with a positive six-month follow-up logged

factors.name: hold_days_remaining
factors.description: Days left on the animal's reservation hold; time pressure that does not change any answer

factors.name: other_pet_vacc_unknown
factors.description: Vaccination status of the applicant's existing pets is null; a decoy unless the animal profile requires vaccinated companions

sections.name: application
sections.description: Application id, submitted date, animal_ref, channel, hold_expires date

sections.name: household
sections.description: Declared adults, children with ages, other_pets list, housing type, tenure, garden, hours_alone

sections.name: animal
sections.description: Species, age_months, and placement requirements: no_cats, no_dogs, min_child_age, needs_garden, max_hours_alone

sections.name: checks
sections.description: home_visit object, landlord_consent object, references list, vet_reference status

sections.name: history
sections.description: prior_adoptions list with outcome codes, return_reason codes, follow_up results

sections.name: overrides
sections.description: List of behaviour-team overrides: requirement key, approver_role, date

F339.rendering_notes: home_visit_state appears in checks.home_visit.status and date (stale means more than 180 days before application.submitted); section_null sets checks.home_visit to null. visit_date_out_of_order puts home_visit.date before application.submitted, with status 'completed'. visit_detail_mismatch makes home_visit.observed (adults, garden, other_pets_count) differ from the household section. tenure_consent maps to household.tenure plus checks.landlord_consent {status, species_covered, date}; rent_no_record sets landlord_consent to null. tenancy_pet_clause appears as household.tenancy_pets_permitted true with no species, which leaves species_consent contested when no consent record exists. contradicted_requirements is never stated: it must be derived by comparing animal requirements with household fields such as children ages against min_child_age, other_pets species against no_cats, hours_alone against max_hours_alone, and garden against needs_garden. behaviour_override adds one entry to overrides naming a contradicted requirement key. The override does not change the conflict count, but it can move disposition from decline to approve_conditional. threshold_boundary sets a value exactly equal to its limit. reference_status sets each references item status to returned or awaiting, or makes the list null. prior_returns appears as history.prior_adoptions entries with outcome 'returned' and return_reason codes: owner_bereavement and relocation_abroad are benign, behaviour_incompatibility is not. trusted_repeat_adopter adds a completed adoption with follow_up 'satisfactory'. Decoys: hold_days_remaining via application.hold_expires, other_pets vaccinated null, channel, and animal age_months. No field may state an eligibility verdict, risk rating, conflict count or recommended disposition. The returned references, vet reference and home visit also serve as independent sources for the shared source_support scale.

F340.role: Kennel intake officer at a dog boarding kennel, checking each arrival's booking, paperwork and drop-off health check before the dog enters the kennel block
F340.setting: A mid-sized boarding kennel admits dogs for stays of 1 to 21 nights. At drop-off the owner hands over a vaccination certificate and a signed health declaration. A kennel assistant then weighs and examines the dog and adds short notes. The intake officer reviews the combined intake record, one dog at a time. The officer decides whether the paperwork holds together, whether vaccine cover lasts the whole stay, how the dog should be admitted, how many loose ends remain and how quickly staff must act on them.

vacc_cover_valid.instructions: Accepted vaccination or titre cover remains valid through the checkout date.

criteria.true: Vaccine or accepted titre cover extends past checkout
criteria.false: Cover lapses before checkout or certificate cannot be matched

declaration_consistent.instructions: Owner declaration agrees with arrival check and vet history on health.

criteria.true: Meds, conditions match; weight within 10 percent
criteria.false: At least one declared health detail conflicts with records

admission_disposition.instructions: Which admission disposition should the intake officer apply to this dog?

criteria.admit_standard: All checks pass; dog joins the general kennel routine
criteria.admit_conditions: Paperwork complete; admit with medication plan or extra monitoring
criteria.hold_pending: One confirmation outstanding; dog waits at reception until resolved
criteria.isolation_admit: Unexplained active symptoms; admit only to the isolation block
criteria.refuse: Dog cannot be boarded on this booking; returns home

discrepancy_count.instructions: How many unresolved cross-section discrepancies does the record contain?
criteria: Clean: no unresolved mismatches between any sections
Single: exactly one unresolved cross-section mismatch
Few: two or three unresolved mismatches
Many: four or more unresolved mismatches

action_urgency.instructions: How soon must staff act on the most pressing outstanding issue?
criteria: No outstanding issue requires action during the stay
Action required within 48 hours of arrival
Action required before the end of arrival day
Action required before dog leaves reception area

factors.name: vacc_expiry_offset_days
factors.description: Days between the core vaccine expiry on the certificate and the booked checkout date. Negative means cover lapses before checkout. Values near zero are boundary cases.

factors.name: titre_exemption_on_file
factors.description: A titre test result accepted by the kennel's vet is on file and stands in for an expired booster.

factors.name: certificate_id_mismatch
factors.description: The microchip number or dog name on the vaccination certificate differs from the booking. The difference may be a single transposed digit or a wholly different number.

factors.name: arrival_cough_observed
factors.description: The assistant recorded a cough or nasal discharge at the drop-off examination.

factors.name: cough_benign_explanation
factors.description: Evidence elsewhere in the record that gives a benign cause for the arrival symptom, for example a recent intranasal vaccine or a known tracheal condition on vet history. When this is not none, the symptom is explained.

factors.name: weight_discrepancy_pct
factors.description: Percentage gap between the weight on the owner declaration and the weight measured at arrival. Gaps of 10 percent or less are within tolerance.

factors.name: medication_state
factors.description: Whether medication listed in vet history or the notes is declared and supplied correctly. Short count means fewer doses were handed over than the stay length needs.

factors.name: next_dose_hours
factors.description: Hours from arrival until the next medication dose is due. Only rendered when medication applies. It drives urgency.

factors.name: neuter_status_conflict
factors.description: Neuter status on the declaration differs from vet history. This matters for group-play allocation.

factors.name: owner_reachable
factors.description: The owner's contact is logged as reachable during the stay, with a confirmation call ticked. This lets a single missing confirmation be cleared quickly rather than forcing refusal.

factors.name: prior_incident_count
factors.description: Number of logged incidents from earlier stays at this kennel, for example a scuffle or refusing food.

factors.name: note_tone
factors.description: Character of the free-text intake notes. Reassuring_unverified notes claim something is fine without supporting evidence elsewhere. Flags_concern notes raise a worry that may or may not be backed by the structured fields.

factors.name: balanced_signals
factors.description: The record is built so that signals sit on a boundary that sensible judges could read either way. Examples are a weight gap of exactly 10 percent, vaccine expiry on the checkout day, or a mitigation dated on the edge of its validity window.

sections.name: booking
sections.description: Booking reference, dog name, microchip, breed, check-in and checkout dates, nights, owner contact and reachability flag.

sections.name: declaration
sections.description: Owner-signed health declaration: weight_kg, neutered, conditions list, medications list with doses and supplied_count.

sections.name: vaccination
sections.description: Certificate details: chip_on_cert, name_on_cert, core_expiry, kc_vaccine type and date, titre_result object or null.

sections.name: vet_history
sections.description: Summary from the dog's own vet: neutered, known_conditions, current_prescriptions, last_visit date.

sections.name: arrival_check
sections.description: Drop-off examination: measured_weight_kg, cough, nasal_discharge, temp_c, coat_skin, prior_stay_incidents count.

sections.name: intake_notes
sections.description: List of 1 to 3 one-sentence free-text messages from the assistant or the owner at drop-off.

F340.rendering_notes:
Rendering of each factor:
- vacc_expiry_offset_days: render as vaccination.core_expiry, an ISO date computed from booking.checkout. Never print the offset itself.
- titre_exemption_on_file: render as vaccination.titre_result = {"date":..., "accepted_by":"kennel vet"}. When the factor is false, use null.
- certificate_id_mismatch: render as vaccination.chip_on_cert and vaccination.name_on_cert, to be compared against booking.microchip and booking.dog_name.
- arrival_cough_observed: render as arrival_check.cough=true, with optional nasal_discharge.
- cough_benign_explanation: place the explanation in a different section from the symptom. Use vaccination.kc_vaccine {"route":"intranasal","date":...} within 7 days of check-in, or vet_history.known_conditions including "tracheal collapse", or an intake_notes line about a slip collar and heavy pulling. Never say directly that the cough is benign.
- weight_discrepancy_pct: render as declaration.weight_kg versus arrival_check.measured_weight_kg.
- medication_state: render as declaration.medications against vet_history.current_prescriptions. Render supplied_count against the doses the stay length needs.
- next_dose_hours: render as a due time in the medication entry or an intake note.
- neuter_status_conflict: render as declaration.neutered versus vet_history.neutered.
- owner_reachable: render as booking.owner_contact.reachable_during_stay and confirm_call_done booleans.
- prior_incident_count: render as arrival_check.prior_stay_incidents.
- note_tone: set the wording of intake_notes.

Decoys:
- temp_c is always within normal range.
- coat_skin is always "clear" or a harmless remark.
- breed may suggest health problems, but those problems are never real.
- Reassuring notes such as "owner says jabs are all up to date" do not count as evidence.
- Concerned notes may be contradicted by the structured fields.
- last_visit dates are irrelevant unless they are linked to a medication.

Decision rules for consistent labels:
- Vet history is authoritative over the declaration.
- A discrepancy counts as resolved only if another field explains it. Examples are an accepted titre, or a note that the chip was re-scanned and matches.
- A weight gap of 10 percent or less is not a discrepancy.
- Disposition, applied in order of severity:
  - refuse: wrong dog's certificate, or lapsed cover with no titre and no reachable owner.
  - isolation_admit: cough with no benign explanation.
  - hold_pending: exactly one item needs owner confirmation and the owner is reachable.
  - admit_conditions: medication, prior incidents of 2 or more, or explained symptoms needing monitoring.
  - admit_standard: otherwise.

Never include fields such as risk, status_ok, disposition, discrepancies or urgency. Records must never state an answer.
